subject: Art superscaling on import
raw_subject: Art superscaling on import
description:
We have a set of several thousand legacy items that we are importing into Learnosity that do not have the width and height explicitly listed in the source, so we are creating json that also does not list the height and width. When these items are imported, the art scales to fit the available width of the item. 
We tried importing with class=\"lrn-image-non-responsive\" on the image, and trie removing the empty height and width attributes on the image reference. Neither of those two options worked. The only way I can resize the art is to open item in Edit mode, edit the art, where the actual height and width are populated, and click OK, and the art shrinks to its correct size and I can save. This is not an acceptable workaround due to the sheer number of art files that have to be touched across all of the items (about 1300). 
1. Is there a easy fix that we can include in the json to correct this issue? 
2. Is this a bug that needs to be fixed? 
You can see an item in our Dev Environment - https://author.learnosity.com/org/1252/v1/item/editornew/?ref=983960d9-1521-4daf-aa86-3366a9efb2bc, and I attached a video of how I have to correct the issue manually.

subject: Creating unique activities for each student
raw_subject: Creating unique activities for each student
description:
Hi, 

We are currently looking at expanding our assessments to support randomly selecting questions from an item bank based on question tags. 

In our current setup, we map 1 to 1 an activity with an exam in our system. We handle randomisation then by loading all questions in an activity and then randomly selecting items and passing them when initialising the assessment. 

The limitation of this approach is that questions need to be added to the activity in order to 'count'. 

We want to allow users to specify tags and then generate an assessment from randomly selected items from the question bank and then build a unique activity for each student. 

My question is, are there any potential known issues or limitations in Learnosity related to creating a lot of unique activities? Since with this method, there would be one activity per student, we cant to ensure this wouldn't cause issues? 


Thanks for your help 
David

subject: Feedback Aide - Multi-discrete rubric and UI issue
raw_subject: Feedback Aide - Multi-discrete rubric and UI issue
description:
Hi, 

I have a question regarding the multi-discrete rubric type for Feedback Aide. 

I have attached a video recording aswell to explain

In the rubric editor, you can specify a 'Point range' as "None" or 'Multiple'. When you select 'Multiple', you can add points for each grade for each criteria. 

From my understanding, I was expecting to be able to specify a range like 1 to 10. So I add 1 as first input and 10 as second input. 

I had two expectation for the behaviour and neither seem to be the case so I wanted to clarify

Expected Scenario  #1
When this rubric is passed to Feedback Aide, I would be expecting that if the model thought this grade should be selected for this criteria, it would select the value 1 OR the value 10 since those are the options I passed. 

Actual result
Model returns 7. 

Expected Scenario  #2
If that wasn't the case, I was expecting that the model would return a value between 1 and 10 and then this value would be set in the feedback aide UI. 

Actual result: Model returns 7 as score but nothing is selected in the UI as only options are buttons 1 and 10. 

What I observed was kind of a mixture between the two. The rubric UI allows me to set a range with whatever points I want. However, it seems the model is expecting that all possible point values are set for each grade. 

It works if I set the point range like this 
Criteria 1 - Grade Poor options [1,2]
Criteria 1 - Grade Average options [3,4]
Criteria 1 - Grade Good options [5,6]

But when building my rubric, if I do not specify every incremental point between two numbers and the model happens to return that number, then nothing is selected in the FeedbackAide Rubric UI when viewing the marking results. 

Is this expected behaviour? 

In the attached video, I have also mentioned a UI bug that I am experiencing when entering scores


Thanks, 
David

subject: Brainstorming session: Supporting submission limits in Learnosity
raw_subject: Brainstorming session: Supporting submission limits in Learnosity
description:
Hello!

We’re beginning to explore how we might offer some of the STEM content currently delivered through WebAssign through our Learnosity integration. One of the key capabilities we would need to support is limited, reviewable submissions at the question-part level.

In this context, a submission is a recorded attempt that counts against a configured limit. We currently support three submission models:

* Question-part submission: Each part of a question has its own submission count.

* Whole-question submission: Submitting any part of a question counts as a submission for every part of that question.

* Whole-assignment submission: A submission counts against the entire assignment, regardless of which question parts were answered.

In Learnosity terms, these could be roughly mapped to "question submission", "item submission", and "activity submission".

Regardless of the submission model, the same configured limit applies to every relevant unit across the activity - each question, each item, or the activity as a whole.

For example, consider an activity containing 10 items, each with two multiple-choice questions. The activity allows three submissions per question part. If a student answers and submits only the first question of Item 1, that question should show one of three submissions used. Every other question part should still show zero of three submissions used. If the student submits responses to the first question two more times, then the first question must become disabled and refuse further submissions as all submissions have been used.

Students and instructors must also be able to review the student’s previous submissions, including the responses associated with each attempt.

Our current understanding is that Learnosity does not have a direct equivalent to this submission model. Limiting Check Answer attempts appears to be the closest existing capability, but it may not address the persistence and review requirements described above.

Before we begin designing an implementation, we’d like to validate our understanding and discuss:

* Whether Learnosity already supports any relevant capabilities or implementation patterns

* Which Items API methods and events might support this behavior

* Any important limitations or edge cases we should account for

* How submission history could be stored and presented to students and instructors

Could we schedule a brainstorming session with Rich and anyone else you think would be helpful? Our goal is to identify a viable direction before we commit to an implementation.

Thanks!
Pierce

subject: 2026.1.LTS validation hiding issue with Custom Question
raw_subject: 2026.1.LTS validation hiding issue with Custom Question
description:
We want to use the 2026.1.LTS capability to hide validation data to make sure test takers can't open browser tools and see the correct answers.

We didn't know that implementing this issue breaks the ability of Learnosity to score our question on the back-end (we knew it would on the front end).

Our understanding is that enabling encryption would allow the server-side scoring with no modifications to the scorer.js itself.

EITHER, we need to get that enabled (we understand that we have to reach out to support for that) and understand the impacts of doing this, OR, we get Learnosity to implement the same capabilities for custom questions that they've implemented for Learnosity question types to still be able to do server-side scoring even if it's a custom question.

This is a fairly urgent need.  We can not ignore the validation object for now, but at some point, the security risk will be too high.

custom_fields.value: The customer wanted to use Learnosity 2026.1.LTS's validation hiding to prevent test takers from seeing correct answers via browser tools but found it broke server-side scoring for their custom question. Learnosity support clarified two options: (1) stripping validation data via the Items API config, which disables frontend scoring but preserves server-side scoring for custom questions if scorer.js is implemented properly, and (2) encrypted validation (a new feature enabled by support) that also supports server-side scoring. The customer confirmed understanding and resolved their scorer.js issues. They now seek best practices to minimize payload size after initially exceeding limits. No encrypted validation was enabled yet; support offered to enable it on dev for testing.

subject: clozeformula and clozeformulaV2 dynamic item navigation restores stale response.value and overwrites saved target responses
raw_subject: clozeformula and clozeformulaV2 dynamic item navigation restores stale response.value and overwrites saved target responses
description:
Hello!

We are seeing response corruption when navigating between previously completed dynamic attempts for a `clozeformula` (and clozeformulaV2) Question using the Questions API dynamic navigation methods.

We call:

```
question.dynamic.previousAttempt({
    persist_target_response: true
});
```

The correct dynamic attempt and attempt ID are selected, but the Question’s normalized `response.value` remains populated with the response from the most recent attempt. When navigating again, that stale value is saved over the response belonging to the attempt being left.

### Environment

- Activity ID: `Z93CNRKZQR00U3442W10WPW4Z1BR5X6E`
- Question type: `clozeformula`
- Questions API version reported in the response: `v2.249.4`
- Response ID example: `31014a3a-62ab-4158-b58b-f0e468f86078_04dc960b6ca0370be395977128fc1c3f`
- Question reference: `dc51d91a-fb02-4c80-a615-6c6d68620afb`
- Item reference: `e1bf5080-006c-48ce-9a21-4c2fbeea4ecc`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch Activity `Z93CNRKZQR00U3442W10WPW4Z1BR5X6E` (or any dynamic item that has a clozeformula question).
2. Navigate to the dynamic `clozeformula` Question.
3. Enter a different response for each attempt:
    - Attempt 1: `7`
    - Attempt 2: `8`
    - Attempt 3: `9`
4. Validate each attempt and increment the `feedbackAttempts` counter:

```
question.validate({
    feedbackAttempts: true,
    showCorrectAnswers: true
});
```

5. Confirm the dynamic response data contains:

```
"attempts": [
    {
        "value": ["7"]
    },
    {
        "value": ["8"]
    },
    {
        "value": ["9"]
    }
]
```

6. While viewing attempt 3, call:

```
question.dynamic.previousAttempt({
    persist_target_response: true
});
```

7. Inspect `question.getResponse()` after attempt 2 is selected.
8. Call the same method again to navigate from attempt 2 to attempt 1.
9. Inspect `question.getResponse()` again.

### Expected behavior

After navigating from attempt 3 to attempt 2:

```
currentAttemptIndex: 1
response.value: ["8"]
dynamic.attempts[1].value: ["8"]
```

After navigating from attempt 2 to attempt 1:

```
currentAttemptIndex: 0
response.value: ["7"]
dynamic.attempts[0].value: ["7"]
```

The previously saved values for all attempts should remain unchanged.

### Actual behavior

Immediately after navigating from attempt 3 to attempt 2, Learnosity reports:

```
currentAttemptIndex: 1
indexed cloze response "0": "8"
response.value: ["9"]
dynamic.attempts[1].value: ["8"]
```

The correct attempt ID and indexed cloze value are restored, but the normalized `response.value` remains `["9"]` from attempt 3.

I tested with different timeouts to see if this is an asynchronous scoring or timing issue, but the mismatch remains after 40 ms, 80 ms, 250 ms, and 1000 ms delay.

Immediately before navigating from attempt 2 to attempt 1, the stored attempts are still:

```
[
    { "value": ["7"] },
    { "value": ["8"] },
    { "value": ["9"] }
]
```

Immediately after `previousAttempt()` returns, they become:

```
[
    { "value": ["7"] },
    { "value": ["9"] },
    { "value": ["9"] }
]
```

It appears that `previousAttempt()` saves the stale normalized value of `["9"]` into attempt 2 before switching to attempt 1. Attempt 1 is then also only partially restored:

```
currentAttemptIndex: 0
indexed cloze response "0": "7"
response.value: ["9"]
dynamic.attempts[0].value: ["7"]
```

On screen, the math input displays the stale value rather than the response belonging to the selected attempt.

### Additional observations

- The overwrite occurs synchronously inside the `previousAttempt()` call, before the method returns.
- The score, `attempt_scores`, and `feedbackAttemptsCount` do not change, so this does not appear related to asynchronous scoring.
- Calling our validation/presentation logic does not modify the inconsistent response object; the mismatch exists before validation.
- The browser stack trace during the call includes:

```
previousAttempt
updateInstance
clozeFormulaV2.render
createMathEditor
```

- Other Question types we have tested do not exhibit this behavior.
- We have not yet reproduced this scenario using `dynamic.nextAttempt()`. However, because it performs the corresponding dynamic response-preservation operation, we suspect the same behavior may occur when navigating forward between attempts.
- We noticed a recent Questions API release note concerning `clozeformula` responses being silently repopulated after a reattempt. Could this behavior be related? (Version 2.234.25)

### Questions

1. Is this a known issue with `clozeformula` and `persist_target_response`?
2. Is `response.value` expected to update before `previousAttempt()` returns?
3. Is there a supported event or completion signal indicating that a dynamic target response has been fully restored?

We can provide the complete response JSON, console logs, screen recording, and the reproducible Item if needed.

Thank you and please let me know if I can provide any more information.

Best,
Mark Petersen

However, when I inspected the underlying network call directly (https://feedbackaide.learnosity.com/api/sessions/fb47383d-10c4-47a1-8b6c-73ec96d025d9?state=grade&call_context=feedbackaide-headless), it returned a 200 with what seems to be a valid  evaluation_response where score is 0, which would be the expected result for a blank response. I'm attaching the full network response for reference.

Given that the API call succeeds but the grader UI throws a validation error, I wanted to confirm whether this error is expected or if there is a recommended way to handle blank responses when loading the grader UI.

2. A student took an activity with different kinds of questions. One of those questions had "Score with Feedback Aide" enabled, but the student skipped it, leaving it as unattempted. When we later checked via the Items API, a feedbackSessionId was never assigned to that question.

We wanted to confirm if this is the expected behavior — meaning that if a question is left as unattempted on submission, a Feedback Aide session will not be created for it, even if it was configured with "Score with Feedback Aide".

{

subject: Drag-and-drop zoom issue where tables cause drop zones to be unreachable by keyboard
raw_subject: Drag-and-drop zoom issue where tables cause drop zones to be unreachable by keyboard
description:
When zoomed and not reflowing, the drop zones are not reachable by keyboard, making the question unanswerable. We do not want the drop zones in these items to reflow because they spell a word; however, they have to be reachable to answer.

In clozeassociation and imageclozeassociationV2 items with tables, drop zones aren't reflowing when zooming. For the item examples we're sharing here, that lack of reflow is desirable because it is a spelling item where a letter goes into each drop area to spell a word. We want all drop areas for a word to stay horizontally aligned.

However, when zoomed in and not reflowing, the item is no longer answerable in current state.

Steps to recreate:
Preview the Renaissance item f72f38da-6036-4fda-adbb-0eb4efaa43f2 (v5.0).

Zoom browser up to 400%. (Item does not reflow since it's in a table.)

Tab through to try to move an answer into a drop zone. Unable to reach the drop zones.

description:
Hotspot zoom reflow problem due to image text

We created some hotspot items with image text. With exceptions, images of text should not be used; exceptions include very large text such as the alphabet letters that are 40 pt, and cases in which the text couldn't be presented as text: logos, street signs. These Hotspot items currently use images of text and there doesn't seem to be a way to recreate these items to function the same way by using text. The template that allows text to be used this way is called Token Highlight but it is configured to only work well for items with multiple correct answers.

Requested solution: allow Token Highlight to be used for single correct answers so that when the option is checked, it doesn't require the student to deselect an answer in order to choose a different one. We would then move our content from hotspot to the token highlight template

subject: Drag-and-drop (cloze association) color contrast in images of text
raw_subject: Drag-and-drop (cloze association) color contrast in images of text
description:
Answer choices change color in cloze association type items (type 1 and 2) when selected (background becomes dark gray and text is still black). This becomes a WCAG issue when the answer options are images of text as then they usually fail contrast requirements. When answers are regular text, the color scheme is different than for images and doesn't cause contrast issues. It doesn't appear to be an issue in regular multiple choice questions as the color scheme is lighter when the answer option is selected.

Steps to recreate:
Preview Renaissance item cebaa521-03d7-49ad-a528-6bb35cadd8db_v3.0.
Select an answer option.
Desired result: the color scheme to indicate the answer option is selected has contrast that meets WCAG requirements. 

One possible solution would be to have the contrast be the same for images and regular text answer options, but we are open to other solutions.

subject: Issue with Match List Item type
raw_subject: Issue with Match List Item type
description:
Hi Team, can you please look into this potential bug as reported by Discovery Education? Thank you.

**Issue Description:** In all _Matching_ item types, where students drag images to matching images, ReadSpeaker reads extra directions and what appears to be a URL or web-link string alongside response containers. The extra text is not visible on screen.

**Learnosity Item Reference ID:** 0abd4b92-18c5-4aa0-90d6-a33f8c74ac27

**What Our Team Tested and Found**
Investigated this issue and it appears to originate from Learnosity's implementation of the Match List item type. During testing, found that the aria-label for each drop area is generated dynamically by Learnosity based on the content of the corresponding left matching category.

 ![](https://learnositysupport.zendesk.com/attachments/token/Om41tRyZG9CInUUTvA0PcABq1/?name=inlineImage.png)
 ![](https://learnositysupport.zendesk.com/attachments/token/0sb1pw4OnAF3tTz8mPolqq5H1/?name=inlineImage.png)

When the left category contains non-text elements (such as images, lists, tables, or other HTML content), Learnosity inserts the underlying HTML/content into the generated aria-label of drop area. As a result, ReadSpeaker reads additional information including image alt text and HTML-related content.

 ![](https://learnositysupport.zendesk.com/attachments/token/26xEksm5Z9cmcoWrRHgCqmbij/?name=inlineImage.png)
Tested the available accessibility configuration options in Learnosity authoring, including:
- Adding alt text to images
- Adding aria labels to categories


**Result**
The above options do not resolve the issue because Learnosity still builds the drop zone's aria-label from the source content and includes the image element/associated content in the generated label.
Since the aria-label is generated internally by Learnosity and is not controlled by our application, we do not see a feasible fix from our side. This would likely require a change in Learnosity's accessibility implementation for this question type.

subject: How to restore content accidentally overwritten via data API
raw_subject: How to restore content accidentally overwritten via data API
description:
In order to accelerate content creation, our org has had to use an publishing workflow:
1. Publish placeholder activities and items directly from our in-house CMS, via the data API (not passing a user in the `meta`).
2. Author edits items and activities, using the Learnosity authoring site. Sometimes author adds new questions, copy/pastes question content.
3. Automatically add new tags to published activities and items, including placeholders and human-edited objects. 

This has been a little challenging, and there have been a couple times when we've accidentally overwritten human edits when re-publishing or updating existing content.

When we look at the item and activity history on the authoring site, we can see the accidental updates; and we can also see the source JSON for the previous state.

My question is: assuming we know what references were impacted, and exactly when the accidental overwriting happened, is there any way to automate restoring a previous state? It appears I can't access the history using the Data API; is there another API I can use?

I'm mostly using the Ruby SDK for all of my Learnosity API works, but I'd be happy to use Javascript if need be. In an ideal world, I'd be able iterate through a list of Activity refs, and roll back each Activity and referenced Items to their pre-overwrite state.

Here are a few examples (in our prod item bank). Accidental overwrites on these were about 2 weeks ago, I haven't investigated the exact datetime yet.

subject: Response Masking resets question font size to default (Large) after selecting Normal font size
raw_subject: Response Masking resets question font size to default (Large) after selecting Normal font size
description:
Hi Team,

We have identified an issue with **Response Masking** in Learnosity and would like to confirm whether this is expected behavior or a known issue.

## Environment

- **Learnosity Version:** v2026.2.LTS
- **Feature:** Response Masking

## Issue

Our assessment is configured with `"fontsize": "large"` as the default font size.

When a user changes the font size to **Normal** using the Accessibility dialog, the font size is applied correctly across the assessment.

However, after enabling **Response Masking**, only the question and answer options revert to the configured default font size (**Large**), while the shared passage (left panel) continues to use the previously selected **Normal** font size.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch an assessment.
2. Open the Accessibility dialog.
3. Change the font size from **Large** to **Normal**.
4. Verify that both the passage and question are displayed using the **Normal** font size.
5. Enable Response Masking.
6. Observe that only the question and answer options revert to the **Large** font size.

## Expected Result

Response Masking should preserve the user's currently selected accessibility font size.

## Actual Result

- Question and answer options revert to the configured default font size (**Large**).
- No `accessibility:change:fontsize` event is triggered when Response Masking is enabled.

## Technical Investigation

We added a listener for the Assess API accessibility font-size event:

```javascript
itemsApp.on('accessibility:change:fontsize', (...args) => {
  console.log(args);
});
```

This event fires correctly when the learner changes the font size using the Accessibility dialog.

However, no event is fired when Response Masking is enabled.

We also inspected the rendered DOM before and after enabling Response Masking.

### Before Enabling Response Masking

**Class:**

```text
lrn lrn_widget lrn_qr lrn_clearfix lrn_mcq
```

**Computed font size:**

```text
14px
```

### After Enabling Response Masking

**Class:**

```text
lrn-masking lrn_font_size_large lrn lrn_widget lrn_qr lrn_clearfix lrn_mcq lrn_font_size_large
```

**Computed font size:**

```text
17px
```

When Response Masking is enabled, the class `lrn_font_size_large` is added to the question widget, causing the computed font size to increase from **14px** to **17px**.

Since our assessment is configured with `"fontsize": "large"` by default, it appears that enabling Response Masking causes the question widget to fall back to the initial configuration rather than preserving the user's current accessibility font size selection (**Normal**).

## Related Release Note

We also noticed the following release note:

### v1.7.4 – 13th August 2025

> Fixed a bug where changing the font size of the assessment player using the accessibility dialog would not be applied when used together with Annotations API.

Although this release note refers to the **Annotations API** rather than **Response Masking**, the observed behavior appears to be similar, where enabling another feature causes the question widget to be re-rendered and the user's selected accessibility font size is no longer preserved.

## Questions

Could you please confirm:

1. Whether this is expected behavior when Response Masking is enabled.
2. Whether this is a known issue in v2026.2.LTS.
3. Whether this has been fixed in a later release or if there is a recommended workaround.



I've attached:

- Screenshots showing the font size before and after enabling Response Masking.
- A screenshot of the v1.7.4 release note for reference.

Thanks,
Ashwin Gattani

subject: Masking functionality & screen reader users - Critical
raw_subject: Masking functionality & screen reader users - Critical
description:
The experience for assistive technology users has changed within the mask/unmask functionality, introducing a new barrier. 

Original experience: 
•	Screen reader users may be confused by the implementation approach used to convey masked and unmasked states. The implementation does not use programmatic states (ex. aria-pressed). Instead, the accessible name of the element is changed based on state.  (WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value)

Current (new) experience:
•	Screen reader users will be unable to perceive the content of the answer options when utilizing the mask/unmask feature. The user only hears "Mask-answer option." or "Unmask-answer option." They do not hear the Answer item letter (e.g., A, B, C...) or its content at all.  (WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value) (Critical)
o	Note: The screen reader user did hear the Answer item letter and its content in the prior version with the original issues.

custom_fields.value: Screen reader users could not hear multiple-choice answer letters or content when response masking was enabled; only “Mask answer option” or “Unmask answer option” was announced. The issue affected JAWS/Chrome and VoiceOver and delayed test dates for users requiring assistive technology. Investigation initially identified custom ARIA labels and a compatibility problem with the “Visible content is navigable by a screen reader” setting. Engineering confirmed and fixed the conflict while preserving existing custom ARIA labels. The fix is released to the developer version, with a backport to 2026.2.LTS planned for the next sprint. Customers should test the developer version and report unexpected behavior; no content changes are required.

subject: Author Aide Loading Developer
raw_subject: Author Aide Loading Developer
description:
Original ticket raised by Will Griffiths on behalf of Will Griffiths at Learnosity

Affected APIs & Versions

Author Aide API

Issue

Author Aide appears to instantiate additional API instances when generated content is loaded. These newly created instances are currently resolving to latest (developer) versions of the dependent APIs rather than inheriting the version already requested by the parent environment.

As a result, production environments can display console warnings indicating that developer versions of Author API, Questions API, and Question Editor API are being loaded.

Priority Context

This issue results in production environments loading developer-version dependencies and displaying warnings in browser developer tools. While functionality does not appear to be impacted, it creates confusion for users and developers and gives the impression that unsupported API versions are being used in production.

Client Context

The issue was initially highlighted internally after console warnings were observed in production-like environments. Investigation suggests that Author Aide is spawning new API instances using latest (developer) rather than respecting the version already requested by the host environment.

This affects customers consuming Author Aide through their own Author API implementations, as well as users accessing Author Aide through the Author site.

Steps to Replicate

1. Open Author Aide (standalone, via Author API, or through the Author site).
2. Generate or load content within Author Aide.
3. Open browser developer tools and inspect the console.
4. Observe warnings indicating that Author API, Questions API, and Question Editor API are being loaded using developer versions.


Expected Behaviour

Any API instances created by Author Aide should inherit and honor the version already requested by the parent environment.

For example:


- If Author Aide is loaded from an LTS version, any dependent APIs should also use that LTS version.
- If Author Aide is loaded from a specific release version, dependent APIs should use the same release version.


No developer-version warnings should appear in production environments unless a developer version was explicitly requested.

Actual Behaviour

When Author Aide loads generated content, it creates new instances of dependent APIs that resolve to latest (developer).

This causes:


- Author API to load from latest (developer)
- Questions API to load from latest (developer)
- Question Editor API to load from latest (developer)


Console warnings are then displayed indicating that developer versions are being used.

subject: Answer Option Ordering with Dynamic Content (TRUE FALSE)
raw_subject: Answer Option Ordering with Dynamic Content (TRUE FALSE)
description:
Basically, the issue is that there are two feature gaps our old content did not:

You cannot dynamically (at runtime) order your answer options
Across variations of a randomized (dynamic) question, you cannot change the position of the correct answer(s) in the array of answer options. However you can dynamically change the values of the answer options.
For certain (true false in particular) questions that are randomized this becomes an issue because you're basically faced with a choice between having the answer option listed with False before True sometimes, or forcing the answer to always be either True (or vice versa).


The request of learnosity would be that for MCQ questions to add an option that forces the True option to always render on top for students when the MCQ consists of answer options whose values are just True or False (or true or false and probably in any language). Alternatively, you can allow for the valid_response key reference to be dynamic.

While the main focus should be on MCQ with answer options whose values are exclusively True or False (in any language or casing). It would be nice to have general control over answer option ordering in a dynamic way (ie alphabetical, ascending, descending)...
But at a minimum we would like to see this supported for True False.

subject: Berklee Audio Player Feature Request.
raw_subject: Berklee Audio Player Feature Request.
description:
Summary

Berklee has highlighted a need for improvements in the Audio Player functionality within Atomic Assessments/Learnosity. These enhancements would support students requiring accommodations and improve transparency in exams that involve audio components.

Current Behavior

1.	Berklee’s core exams use a 2-part item setup: a passage and an audio player.
2.	The current setup does not allow custom accommodations for the number of audio playbacks, forcing Berklee to create multiple versions of exams for different accommodation needs.
3.	The audio player does not display the playback limit to students. Instructors currently have to include this information manually in the passage text.
Proposed Enhancements

1.	Customizable Play Count Accommodations:
•	Allow instructors to set individualized playback limits for audio players per student or group, directly addressing accommodation requirements.
•	Example: A standard playback limit of 3 for most students, with an accommodation allowing 5 playbacks for select students.
2.	Student Playback Limit Display:
•	Include a visible playback limit on the audio player interface for students.
•	Example: “You have X playbacks remaining out of Y total” or a progress bar/ticker showing the remaining count.
•	This will reduce confusion and eliminate the need for manual instructions in the passage text.
Benefits

•	Simplifies exam setup for instructors, eliminating the need for multiple exam versions.
•	Enhances accessibility for students requiring accommodations.
•	Improves user experience by providing clear feedback to students on playback limits.
Additional Notes

•	This request originates from Berklee, who are key users of Atomic Assessments and Learnosity’s Audio Player.
•	These features would align with Universal Design for Learning (UDL) principles by ensuring equitable access to assessment materials.
Priority

Medium to High. Accommodations and accessibility are critical in academic settings, and these changes would significantly improve the assessment experience for both instructors and students.

subject: Audio Functionality
raw_subject: Audio Functionality
description:
Hello!

We are currently looking to implement new features in our player, regarding the user's media experience, by providing them with custom hardware controls.
Specifically we want to implement:
- Audio Output Selection: Allowing users to switch between headphones and speakers (using .setSinkId()).
- Volume Control: A custom slider to manage playback levels.
- Active Microphone Selection: Forcing a specific device ID for recording.

During our research we noticed that your media players are instantiated in-memory, and are not exposed to the DOM. This encapsulation prevents us from using standard Web APIs to target the media elements for hardware routing or volume management.
Does Learnosity currently offer any official APIs or recommended workarounds to handle these features programmatically?
If not, would you be open to implementing support for this? Exposing methods like setAudioDevice(deviceId) and setVolume(level), or providing a lifecycle event that returns the HTMLMediaElement reference would be great for our usecase.

Thanks, Fede.

subject: Feature Inquiry: Customize Parallel Symbol to Japanese Standard (//) in Cloze Math and Custom Question Types
raw_subject: Feature Inquiry: Customize Parallel Symbol to Japanese Standard (//) in Cloze Math and Custom Question Types
description:
Hi Learnosity Support Team,

We are reaching out to inquire about the feasibility of customizing the display 
and input behavior of the parallel symbol within the Learnosity math editor, 
specifically to align with Japanese mathematical notation standards.

---

## Background

In international standards, the parallel sign is rendered as a straight symbol (∥).
However, in Japan's mathematics curriculum, the parallel sign is conventionally rendered as italic double slashes (//).

As we serve Japanese clients, it is essential 
that our question content reflects this local convention to avoid confusion or scoring errors for students.

---

## Scope of Request

We would like to apply this customization to the following two contexts:

1. Learnosity Native Question Type
   - Cloze Math (`clozemath`)
   - Specifically the key visual in the math keyboard, and rendering layer used in the response input and authored content display (refer attached pic)

2. Manabie Custom-Developed Question Type
   - We have a custom question type built on top of Learnosity's Custom Question Type API
   - We would like to apply the exact same symbol customization as #1 within this custom type as well

---

## Question

We would appreciate your guidance on the possible customization solution for the above mentioned 2 question types.

---

## Priority & Context

This is currently a blocker for Japanese Language Math content authoring for one of our partner schools. We are in active content migration and would appreciate an early indication of feasibility before committing to a 
custom implementation path.

---

Thank you for your support in advance.

Best regards,

subject: Accessibility issue at 320px viewport width in Cloze Math keyboard
raw_subject: Accessibility issue at 320px viewport width in Cloze Math keyboard
description:
Hi Learnosity Team,

I’m reaching out to report a accessibility issue affecting the math symbol keyboard on our student launch experience.

Issue summary
When the page is viewed at a viewport width of 320 CSS pixels, some content in the math input symbol keyboard disappears. Examples include symbols such as “x”, “y”, etc. This appears to be a reflow/responsive behavior issue and may prevent users from accessing required functionality.

WCAG criteria

WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.4.10 Reflow
Conformance Level: AA

User impact
Users with low vision who need to resize text or use narrow viewports may be unable to perceive or access content and functionality because symbols disappear at 320 CSS pixels.

Actual result
At 320 CSS pixels wide, content in the symbol keyboard disappears. Observed examples include:

“x”
“y”
other math symbols


Expected result
At a viewport width of 320 CSS pixels, all content and functionality should remain available without loss of information or functionality and without requiring two-dimensional scrolling, except where an allowed WCAG exception applies.

Recommendation
Please ensure the component reflows properly at 320 CSS pixels so that all symbols and controls remain visible and operable. Moving overflow content into an accessible show/hide control, such as a hamburger or “more symbols” menu, would be acceptable if implemented accessibly.

subject: Accessibility Issue – Illogical Focus Order in Drag & Drop Interaction (WCAG 2.4.3)
raw_subject: Accessibility Issue – Illogical Focus Order in Drag & Drop Interaction (WCAG 2.4.3)
description:
We have identified an accessibility issue in the drag-and-drop interaction where the keyboard focus order is not logical after selecting an option.

When a user activates a draggable option, the visual highlight moves to the response input field, but the keyboard focus does not follow, leading to confusion and inconsistent interaction.

User Impact:
Keyboard-only users cannot follow the interaction flow properly
Users may get confused as visual focus and keyboard focus are not synchronized
Extra navigation (Shift + Tab) is required to reach the intended drop target
This creates a poor and inefficient user experience, especially for assistive technology users
Environment Details:
OS: Windows 11 (23H2 - 22631.5624)
Browser: Chrome 140.0.7339.208 / Edge 40.0.3485.66
Platform: Scholastic Learning Zone
Steps to Reproduce:
Book - 
Amazing MakerSpace DIY Slippery Slime
by Cody Crane
Click Next until reaching Question 2 (Drag & Drop interaction)
Select any drag-and-drop option
Use Tab key to navigate forward
Use Shift + Tab to navigate backward
Observe focus behavior
Actual Result:
On activating a drag-and-drop option:
The response input field gets visually highlighted
However, keyboard focus does NOT move to it
When navigating backward using Shift + Tab, focus lands on the response input field
Pressing Enter then performs the drop action
This results in:
Inconsistent and non-intuitive focus behavior
Expected Result:
When a drag-and-drop option is activated:
Keyboard focus should automatically move to the response input field
Pressing Enter should directly complete the drop action
Focus order should:
Follow a logical and predictable sequence
Match the visual flow of interaction
Note:
This issue is reproducible across all drag-and-drop options on the page
WCAG Reference:
2.4.3 – Focus Order

description:
Original ticket raised by Michael Fares on behalf of Michael Fares at Learnosity

**Affected APIs & Versions**

Data API all versions

**Issue**

When showing scores for a submitted activity, The Data API sessions/responses payload contains no data/flags indicating whether the scores were due to points overrides at authoring time.

**Priority context**

**Client Context**

**Steps to Replicate**


1. Create an activity with no point overrides at first. Submit the activity via Items API and then check the Data API sessions/responses payload .
2. With the same activity, override the point values for any item (e.g change Item 1 from 1pt to 2pts). Submit a new session and check the Data API sessions/responses payload for it.
3. Compare the Data API sessions/responses payload for both sessions, as in this example diff: https://www.diffchecker.com/ybB7RLyK/

**Expected Behaviour**

If an activity has had it's item or question scores overriden, then the Data API sessions/responses payload when assigning those score should also include some information that they were overriden and possibly what the default score was otherwise.

**Actual Behaviour**

The Data API sessions/responses payload contains no data/flags indicating whether a submitted activity's scores were due to points overrides at authoring time or not.

This has the possibility to result in unneeded confusion for customers and / or support in situations where a customer may be looking at sessions/responses data and confused about why in session 1 item A >  has a score of 1 point but in session 2 the same item A has a score of 5 points. Without knowing that an author overrode points in between the 2 sessions the customer will have no clear way know determine the reason for this otherwise.

subject: Item Points Override and Bulk Activity Edit performance concern
raw_subject: Item Points Override and Bulk Activity Edit performance concern
description:
Hello,

Cengage is considering adopting the new item points override feature, and we would appreciate your feedback on the following use case.

A Cengage course may contain as many as 3,000 LRNO activities in a single semester. We support a workflow that allows an instructor to bulk update the total activity points for all 3,000 activities. Our requirement is that the item points be scaled proportionally from the existing activity point total to the new activity point total, using the same scaling factor for each item. Cengage would then update the item point overrides through DataAPI.

A few concerns came up during our discussion:

1) DataAPI would receive copy requests for all 3,000 activities, subject to the limit of 50 requests every 5 seconds. Since the job is asynchronous, do we know the typical processing time for large activity copy operations? This could affect how we design the frontend experience for bulk points editing if the wait time is significant.

2) After the copy completes, AuthorAPI would perform a filtered retrieval that includes both the original activities and the newly copied activities. This means the initial bank retrieval activity search would return 6,000 records before filtering. Are there any performance concerns with AuthorAPI search and filtering at that scale?

3) Does DataAPI support item points override directly, without going through the AuthorAPI UI? If so, that could materially affect the implementation approach we take for this workflow.

We expect it would be rare for an instructor to bulk update the activity point total for all 3,000 activities. However, since the Cengage platform does allow this workflow, we want to do our due diligence and understand whether there are any performance or scalability concerns.

Thanks,
--Wilson

description:
Hello,

We have a client who would like to use the Video Recorder solution as part of their admissions process, but they are encountering two issues that could potentially jeopardize the deal.

1. They do not want candidates to be able to re-record their video; only a single recording attempt should be allowed.

description:

Question:
When playing a random activity in Items API, or fetching the session responses from Data API, is it possible to know which Item Group an item was served from?

Background:
We're building the capability for authors to set how many points each item in an activity is worth. We've run into an issue with random activities as we'd like to set how many points each item group is worth and then divide the points amongst the "picked" items.

Basically, if we knew which item group an item was served from, then we could persist the points possible against the item group ID and distribute the points amongst the "picked" items, easily allowing us to handle decimal points. However, if we can't, then we have to instead persist the points possible against each item in the group so that the "picked" items' points possible values would sum to the item group total. The issue is that this makes the decimal points handling very difficult.

Thanks!
Pierce

subject: Increase Session Metadata size limit?
raw_subject: Increase Session Metadata size limit?
description:
Hello!

Is it possible to raise the session metadata size limit from 10,000 bytes to something higher?

Problem: We're looking into how we can support the ability to add item weights to activities. In other words, our instructors need the ability to set how many points each item should be worth, without the need of modifying content. 

Our thought is that we'd pass this item weight data through the session metadata object on Items API init so that when our analytics system fetches the session data from Data API when a session update event is emitted from the AWS Kinesis Data Firehose, that they'd be able to pull the item weight data from the session metadata.

The problem? The item weight data is a simple map of item reference ID to a point value. Assuming all item reference IDs are uuidv4s and the longest point value would be something like 999.99, then we would max out at 217 items that we would be able to account for. We also place some other data in the session metadata, which would lower the amount of items we would be able to support at once.

While an activity with >200 items is arguably a bad learning experience, we do have activities in use today that are larger.

Thanks!
Pierce

subject: RTE input prevents consecutive $ characters
raw_subject: RTE input prevents consecutive $ characters
description:
Original ticket raised by Stephen Sayage on behalf of Stephen Sayage at Learnosity

**Affected APIs & Versions**
Author API, Question Editor API, RTE
Tested from 2024.1.LTS to latest

**Client's API Version**
 Issue found internally

**Issue**
There appears to be an issue in the Rich Text Editor (RTE) where entering consecutive `$` characters is not allowed in any RTE input field.

This behavior does not appear related to the recent bug fix (LRN-48428) for supporting `$$` as a LaTeX delimiter in the UI, which was included in 2025.1.LTS-latest. Testing shows that:

- The consecutive `$` issue occurs even on 2024.3.LTS, which predates the `$$` delimiter patch.
- The `$$` delimiter functionality does not work on 2024.3.LTS, which leads me to believe that the consecutive `$` issue is independent of the delimiter patch.

**Priority context**
Low

**Client Context**
Reported internally

**Steps to Replicate**
https://labs.learnosity.com/demos/api-author/author.php
Set version to 2024.3.LTS

- Open any item or create a new one.
- Using any input field that uses the RTE - attempt to enter consecutive `$` characters (e.g., `$$`).
- Observe that the second `$` is either stripped or blocked.

**Expected Behaviour**
Consecutive `$` characters should be allowed in the RTE

**Actual Behaviour**
Consecutive `$` characters are blocked in the RTE

**Developer Suggestion**

subject: Ensure radio button groups are properly formed
raw_subject: Ensure radio button groups are properly formed
description:
Hi Team,

We’ve identified accessibility issues across various item types, including but not limited to Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs):

Issue
Radio button groups and other interactive controls are not programmatically associated with their question text. For example, when a screen reader user navigates to a radio button or similar control, the question (e.g., “What is the correct spelling?”) is not announced. Instead, the screen reader only announces the option label or a hardcoded response, making it difficult for users to understand the context.
This issue affects MCQs and other question types where options are presented as grouped controls.

Impact
This behaviour does not comply with WCAG 2.1 guidelines:

1.3.1 – Info and Relationships
4.1.2 – Name, Role, Value

Form controls must be properly linked to their labels and grouped questions so that assistive technologies can convey the correct context.

Required Fix

Ensure all grouped controls (radio buttons, checkboxes, etc.) are programmatically associated with their question text.
Use:

A shared name attribute for radio button groups.
Semantic HTML (<fieldset> and <legend>) or ARIA attributes (aria-labelledby), so the question is announced when the group receives focus.


Apply similar fixes for other item types to ensure consistent accessibility compliance.

This change will improve usability for screen reader users and ensure WCAG compliance.

Additional Request
Please create a Learnosity Help account for:
Aniket Anand
Email: Aniket.Anand@powerschool.com

subject: Performance degradation and High CPU usage in Item activity editor
raw_subject: Performance degradation and High CPU usage in Item activity editor
description:
Hi LRN Support Team,

We would like to report a performance issue that has been raised by multiple users and is now significantly impacting daily usage.

1. Context
We are embedding Learnosity into our system, where our users manage content by creating and updating questions within activities.

2. Reported Issues from Users
Our users have consistently reported the following problems:
- The question content takes a long time to load and display in the Review tab.
- After working in an activity for approximately 10-20 minutes, their laptops begin to overheat, the fan becomes louder, and CPU usage spikes to 100%.
-> As a result, the browser becomes very slow, laggy, or completely frozen.
- In many cases, users are forced to restart their laptops in order to continue working.
This behavior is causing significant disruption, inconvenience, and frustration, as it interrupts their daily workflow.

3. Reproduction and Verification
I have personally tested this issue and encountered the same behavior (please see the attached recording for reference, you can also hear the loud fan sound).
You can reproduce the issue using the following activities:
01JN6DCDPSYDF3F0PN369JDCQY
01JN6DCDPSYDF3F0PN39B0H05F
01JN6DCDPSYDF3F0PN357GNS04

In these activities, repeatedly switching between the Edit and Review tabs reliably triggers the performance degradation on my laptop, consistent with what our users have reported.
While we cannot confirm whether all activities are affected, the issue is reproducible and consistent in the activities listed above.


4. Request
We kindly ask that this issue be thoroughly investigated, including analysis of CPU usage, memory consumption, and any potential rendering or event-handling problems. Given the severity of the impact on end users, we would appreciate identifying the root cause and understanding what steps can be taken to prevent this behavior going forward.
Please let us know if you need any additional information from our side to assist with the investigation.


Thank you for your support, and we look forward to your findings.

Best regards,

subject: Reports API Session Limit
raw_subject: Reports API Session Limit
description:
Hello!
We frequently use the Reports API to summarize a class's activity; either based on an "assignment" (shared activityID) or based on an Item's categorization (such as, all items related to Supply and Demand). In either of these cases, it's very common for the amount of sessions to exceed 100. It is not atypical for our university courses to have classes of over 200 students.
The documentation states:

subject: Accessibility: Disabled layout elements are focusable via keyboard
raw_subject: Accessibility: Disabled layout elements are focusable via keyboard
description:
Hi Learnosity Team,

We have identified an accessibility issue with the disabled (non-interactive) layout elements (e.g., "Five-sixths" and "Three-fourths" blocks from attached image) are exposed in the tab order and receive keyboard focus. They are not operable, yet screen reader and keyboard users can land on them.
This creates ambiguity: users encounter a focusable element with no actionable purpose or clear semantic, increasing cognitive load and impairing efficient navigation.

Question Type: Cloze with drop down

Observed Screen Reader Behavior:
1. Focus moves to the disabled, non-interactive elements.
2. Users cannot act on the element and may think something is broken.
3. Users will be unable to determine its purpose.

Akshay

subject: Security Alert: Cheating Script Targeting Learnosity Assessments (AI21 API Key Exposed)
raw_subject: Security Alert: Cheating Script Targeting Learnosity Assessments (AI21 API Key Exposed)
description:
I am writing to bring to your attention a critical security concern identified via CrowdStrike Recon

Summary of Issue:
A GitHub user, AFRIENDLYHACKER (IHACK4FUN), has published a browser-based cheating script in a public repository:
https://github.com/AFRIENDLYHACKER/uhhhhh-idkj/blob/main/index.js

The script is a sophisticated browser-based cheating tool targeting Schoology assessments, including those powered by Learnosity.

It automates answer extraction, quiz completion, and assessment manipulation by intercepting Learnosity API calls and DOM scripting.

Features include:

Reveal Answer (from Learnosity API and DOM)

Auto Fill/Complete

Extract All Data (including question metadata, scoring, standards)

AI Solve (using exposed AI21 Studio Jamba API key)

Simulated Human Behavior (random delays, mouse movements)

The script exposes an AI21 API key in public, enabling unauthorized use of external AI services to solve proprietary educational content.

This activity undermines assessment integrity, exposes confidential data, and constitutes unauthorized use of a customer environment.

subject: Can there be a default value automatically entered in all response boxes on a Clozetext question?
raw_subject: Can there be a default value automatically entered in all response boxes on a Clozetext question?
description:
We're using ClozeText questions to create transaction analysis questions for a Financial Accounting course. An example question is the one with rich-test-book-7-5-23_ch01.01q69 as the learnosity ID. 

There is a grid, and most of the values in the question are 0, with some responses set to other values depending on the specific transactions that students are asked to enter. The instructor for the course would like to have the question start off with all values set to 0, so that students don't have to manually enter all the zeros. There is a setting under More Options>Layout which is called "Placeholder". When 0 is entered into this box, a kind of 'ghost zero' is entered in each response box of the question. It is grayed out, but when a user clicks on a particular response box, the cursor is still at the beginning of the box, and responses that have not had a value manually entered still receive no credit. It seems like, if this placeholder value could be made something that is actually entered in the boxes, we might achieve what we're aiming at.

The goal is to end up with a system where all response boxes initially have a 0 entered in them when students open the question, and students replace that with the required value where appropriate, but they don't have to manually enter zeros into each box that should be empty/have a value of zero.

subject: copying an item and immediately assigning it to an activity sometimes shows error placeholder
raw_subject: copying an item and immediately assigning it to an activity sometimes shows error placeholder
description:
Hi,


We added some logic to the activity authoring view, so we can copy existing items and add it to the active activity. However, often times when the view refreshes after linking the item to the activity, we see the error "This Activity contains restricted or missing Items. The information in those items is not available or shown in the preview." (see attached screenshot). After saving the activity with this duplicated item and refreshing the page, we see the copied item correctly displayed.

The flow currently works as follows:
- Duplicate the item through the api call `itembank/items/duplicate` with the payload `{ items: [{ reference: 'source-guid', new_reference: 'new-guid' }]`.
- After the api call completes, we explicitly wait 1 second.
- Update the authoring view by adding the new item to the activity through `AuthorApp.setActivityItems([{ id: 'source-guid', reference: 'source-guid' }, { id: 'new-guid', reference: 'new-guid' }])`.

To be fair, this error does not always happen (presumable because of the 1s delay), just more frequently than what it used to be. Is there a way to prevent this warning? I.e. polling the item endpoint to ensure it's available before attaching it to the activity? Or can you suggest a better solution?


Kind regards,
Thomas

subject: Accessibility Issue - Accessible Name for Combobox
raw_subject: Accessibility Issue - Accessible Name for Combobox
description:
Hello Learnosity Team,

We've identified an accessibility issue with the combobox component. The combobox currently has an insufficiently descriptive accessible name. It is programmatically labeled as "Response input area", which does not provide enough context regarding its purpose.

Issue Details:
The visual labels for the comboboxes, such as "What is the word form of Fraction A?" and "What is the word form of Fraction B?", are not reflected in the programmatic label, which remains "Response input area" for both. This discrepancy could confuse screen reader users, as the accessible name doesn't align with the visible prompt.

Impact:
Screen reader users are unable to understand the combobox's 
function. For instance, they would not know that the dropdown is used to select the number of equal parts in a fraction bar.


WCAG Success criteria:
2.5.3 - Label in Name
2.4.6 - Headings and Labels

WCAG Conformance level:  
A (2.5.3)
AA (2.4.6)

Disabilities Affected:
Visual, Physical, Neurological

Would it be possible to update the aria-label for the combobox to ensure it's more descriptive and aligned with the visual labels?

I tried looking into toolbar which shows up at each stems or answers but it doesn't have a way to update aria labels.

If this is something that can be adjusted through settings or component properties, we'd appreciate any guidance you can provide.

Thank you,
Akshay

subject: Not Authoring UI to set Annotation API's Highlighter element when using custom player template
raw_subject: Not Authoring UI to set Annotation API's Highlighter element when using custom player template
description:
_Opening on behalf of Edward Lynch from ZD Ticket #28875_

> We often use custom player templates. We are not seeing Hightlighter/Highlighting as an option. We offer highlighting in all of our forms. How do we turn that on if we are using a custom player template?



Workaround:

> It's because the Annotation API's Highlighter isn't something you add to the regions of the player template (which is why you don't see it as one of the elements). Therefore, you'll need to add it in the 'Source' Tab:
>
> - annotations
> - annotations_api_init_options
>
> "annotations": true,"annotations_api_init_options": { "modules": { "texthighlight": true }}


Action: Raise to engineers

subject: Screen Reader Issue: Inappropriate use of table when creating stacked equations with LaTeX/MathJax
raw_subject: Screen Reader Issue: Inappropriate use of table when creating stacked equations with LaTeX/MathJax
description:
Hi Alanna,

As mentioned in #28813, I am splitting the issues raised therein into different tickets so we can better monitor progress.

This ticket deals with the issue below:


> The subtraction problem (100 − 53) is coded within a table structure, and the screen reader announces table roles such as “row, column” while reading the content. This adds irrelevant complexity and confuses users.
>
> Sample Item: Grade 2 Unit 4 Form A Item 4.
>
> Login Instructions:
>
> 1. Open the product Math Expressions, Grades K–6 California Core Math Curriculum.
> 2. Select Grade 2.
> 3. Navigate to Unit 4.
> 4. Open the Unit Assessment.
> 5. Select Form A Test.
> 6. Go to question 4
>
> Navigate the page using the down arrow key with the screen reader. Observe that the subtraction problem (100 − 53) is coded within a table structure.
>
> WCAG Guideline Number: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships – Level A
>
> Actual Result:
>
> The subtraction problem (100 − 53) is coded within a table structure, and the screen reader announces table roles such as “row, column” while reading the content. This adds irrelevant complexity and confuses users.
>
> Rationale:
>
> Screen readers interpret the subtraction problem as a table with rows and columns, which is misleading and creates unnecessary verbosity
>
> Recommendation:
>
> Do not use <table> for layout or visual alignment of math problems.

> Expected Result:
> The subtraction expression should be announced as a mathematical equation only (e.g., “100 minus 53”) without extraneous references to tables, rows, or columns.


Example affected item: author.learnosity.com/v1/item/editornew/?ref=1000403517

This affects questions where an author has created a stacked equation in LaTeX with the Learnosity Math Editor. LaTeX and mathematical content rely upon a third-party library, MathJax, to translate LaTeX and mathematical markup into a structure a web browser can parse and understand. It appears that Mathjax, in order to render the stacked equation in the browser, uses a table element to structure the equation. This is being read as a data table by the screen reader and this is causing the confusing instructions.

It is normally possible to apply an aria-label to any LaTeX created with the math editor, like in the image below:

 ![](https://learnositysupport.zendesk.com/attachments/token/0gN1bFSTac9EzGZllgUUSRitE/?name=Screenshot+2025-10-10+at+19.20.11.png)

However, I found that the table is still read aloud even after the aria-label is applied and I have raised this issue with the accessibility team.  But - as it is being created by a third party library - it may not be possible to remove the table element entirely.

If you are seeking a workaround: you could consider removing the stacked equation and using different LaTeX (MathJax uses different elements for non-stacked equations). Another approach would be to use an image of a stacked equation rather than LaTeX. Images uploaded to Learnosity LTS version 2025.1 and later will have alt-text automatically generated for them which can reduce the burden on authors.

I shall monitor the progress of this issue and update this ticket once I have information from the team. Let me know if you have any questions.

Regards,

Chris

subject: Screen Reader announces superfluous 'blank' or 'selected a' when focus is on response box
raw_subject: Screen Reader announces superfluous 'blank' or 'selected a' when focus is on response box
description:
Hi Alanna,



> Screen reader announces unnecessary “selected a” when focusing on the response input area.
>
> Sample Item: Grade 6 End of Year Test Item 1 [Found in Program Assessments]
>
> Navigate the page using the keyboard with the screen reader. Observe that the screen reader announces unnecessary “a” when focusing on the response input area.
>
> WCAG Guideline Reference: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships – Level A
>
> Actual Result:
>
> Screen reader announces unnecessary “selected a” when focusing on the response input area.
>
> Rationale:
>
> The extra “selected a” causes confusion for screen reader users, as it provides misleading information.
>
> Recommendation:
>
> Ensure that the no redundant characters is announced while announcing the Input edit field.
>
> Expected Result:
>
> Screen reader should announce only “Response area edit multi line” (without the extra “a”).



> Screen reader announces both edit fields correctly, but after reading them, it also announces an unnecessary “blank”
>
> Sample Item: Grade 6 End of Year Test Item 1 [Found in Program Assessments]
>
> Navigate the page using the down arrow key with the screen reader. Observe that the screen reader announces unnecessary blank space.
>
> WCAG Guideline Reference: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships – Level A
>
> Actual Result:
>
> Screen reader announces both edit fields correctly, but after reading them, it also announces an unnecessary “blank”.
>
> Rationale:
>
> Redundant or unclear announcements create confusion for screen reader users.
>
> Recommendation:
>
> Ensuring no hidden or extra label/placeholder is programmatically exposed.
>
> Expected Result:
>
> Screen reader should announce only the two available edit fields with their proper labels


Example Item: https://author.learnosity.com/v1/item/editornew/?ref=1000403030


I was not able to replicate the latter  (screen reader reading an unnecessary 'Blank') but I was able to replicate the former (unnecessary 'selected a'). Nevertheless, I believe both issues stem from the same cause.

Upon inspection, the browser is inserting a superfluous character as a shadow element which is set as a child element of the response box. This is what the screen reader is reading aloud when is says 'blank' or 'selected a'.


However, I could only replicate this with the formulaV2 question-type. This is a deprecated question type and has been deprecated since the release of LTS version v2022.1. It is recommended to use `clozeformula` or `clozeformulaV2` instead. Deprecation means there will be no further improvements or development work carried out on this question. Given this, it is worth considering re-authoring to use a support question-type such as `clozeformula` or the newer `clozeformulaV2`.

I tested with a newer question-type (`clozeformula`) and could not replicate. Please see the video attached. Given this, I think the best approach would be to re-author with supported question-type.

I hope this was helpful. Let me know if you have questions.

Regards,

Chris

subject: Can graphing questions ignore leading/trailing spaces in labels?
raw_subject: Can graphing questions ignore leading/trailing spaces in labels?
description:
At present, graphing questions that include labels require that the labels be identical to the set answer, including having no leading/trailing spaces if the set answer doesn't. Since graphing questions don't allow partial credit, and this is something that students do inconsistently, if a question has multiple labels, you'd need to add a bunch of alternate answers to account for the various combinations of extra spaces that might be added. If the labels instead ignored leading and trailing spaces in labels, this would be preferable. 

Similarly, if it's possible to set it up so that labels can ignore capitalization that would be fantastic, but I realize that may be something that would need to be submitted separately. 

For an example of a question where this is an issue, see learnosity question Rittenberg_PoEv5_ch04.02q05. 

A student answered it in session 3579967b-d887-44ad-924f-bf0e315a74f4 where it was the 6th question on that assignment, with an extra trailing space after the 2023 equilibrium label.

subject: Reports API Reports Data - Retrieving Options Information for Rating Type Questions
raw_subject: Reports API Reports Data - Retrieving Options Information for Rating Type Questions
description:
Hello!

I have a question regarding expected behavior/format for the Report Data retrieved from Reports API, specifically for Rating type questions.

For some background, in our front-end app, we are initializing Reports API and retrieving the `reportsData` object that comes from the `dataListener` callback. For various reasons, we need to parse through this data ourselves to retrieve information about session responses and the question data itself. Essentially, we want to match each take (and the user of that take) to one of the possible response values for a question. To do this, we need to know all the possible response choices for a question as well as what selection each user chose. Reports API provides all this information for us, except in a particular case for Rating type questions.

When it comes to another question type like Multiple Choice, we have all the data that we need, as shown in one of my screenshot attachments taken from a debug view. In `reportsData`, we can access the `questions[index].options` array which contains all the possible response values, which is exactly what we need.

However, when it comes to the Rating type question, it appears that Reports API does not provide this `options` array, as shown in my second screenshot of a rating type question. Here, we are given the `permutations` of what users chose, which works fine if each response option was selected by at least one student. But in the event that an option was not selected by any students, then there doesn't appear to be a way to reliably find all the possible option choices for a rating question in the same way that this is possible for a multiple choice question.

Is this expected behavior/format for the `reportData` retrieved from Reports API? As it currently stands, we are running into the issue of not being able to retrieve all possible response choices for a rating type question from the data retrieved from Reports API. We do have some ideas of a workaround for this, but wanted to check in with the Learnosity team first to see if perhaps we are doing something wrong on our end or if there were an easier way to access this data.

Best,
Mark

subject: Re: [Imagine Learning] Update: Accessibility Grouping Issue: Question/Instruction Not Included in Checkbox Group/Answer Options Group for Screen Readers
raw_subject: Re: [Imagine Learning] Update: Accessibility Grouping Issue: Question/Instruction Not Included in Checkbox Group/Answer Options Group for Screen Readers
description:
This is a follow-up to your previous request #28595 "Accessibility Grouping Issu..."

Hi Chris,

 

Can you please forward the message below to your product and engineering teams regarding this issue? Let me know when you hear back.

 

Thank you for your thoughtful response to our reported accessibility issue regarding checkbox answer groupings and their associated instructions. We appreciate your concern about avoiding verbosity for complex stimuli.

 

However, our accessibility testing partner, Level Access, has confirmed that the current implementation does not meet WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships). Specifically:

* Screen reader users entering a checkbox group do not receive the governing instruction, leading to confusion, errors, and increased cognitive load.
* Keeping the instruction visually close but not programmatically associated does not satisfy WCAG, as the relationship must be exposed in the accessibility tree.

 

Recommended fix from Level Access:

* Wrap checkbox groups in a <fieldset> with a concise <legend> containing the operative instruction, or
* Use aria-labelledby on the group container to reference a concise instruction.
* Keep lengthy or complex stimuli outside the group with their own heading/id, optionally adding a link (“Review the stimulus above”) so users can recheck context when needed.

 

This approach ensures compliance and improves usability by giving users both the governing instruction and access to longer stimuli when required.

 

Because the grouping and markup are controlled by Learnosity, this fix needs to be implemented at the platform level rather than by customers. We ask that you reconsider the current decision and plan a remediation that aligns with WCAG requirements and industry best practices.

 

Please let us know how you intend to address this issue, and we are happy to facilitate further testing and validation once a fix is in place.

 

Best regards,
Jon Wills

subject: Additions to graphing question type
raw_subject: Additions to graphing question type
description:
Hi all, 

I have a customer who would like to make use of the graphing question types but has found some limitations. They are for now making use of the drawing question type as it will support them better but as a drawing question cannot be auto-scored, I wanted to explore if there are options to improve functionality on graphing questions. 

They are looking for a way of students drawing graphs as part of an economics exam. Specifically they are looking for the ability to add different coloured lines which represent different increases / decreases in economic value for different countries. Currently, only one colour is being supported on graphing questions and it is therefore not possible to distinguish different outcomes. 

On the drawing question, with the help of uploading an image of a standard graph, the customer can add in different colours that students can use to draw lines on top of the graph to indicate economic changes for different countries (e.g. USA represented by blue lines but EU represented by green lines). 

I acknowledge that it will probably be difficult to add auto-scoring into a drawing question but would it be possible to expand the graphing question types with different colours and, potentially, the option for students to add in some text elements (e.g. naming the x and y axis)?

I am looking forward to your response
Best 
Sabrina
