subject: Cloze_Math question type: Screen reader (NVDA) repeats correct answer announcement twice
raw_subject: Cloze_Math question type: Screen reader (NVDA) repeats correct answer announcement twice
description:
When authoring a Cloze_Math question,NVDA screen reader announces the correct option twice when previewed. Steps to Reproduce 1. Author a Cloze_Math question with the following JSON in the source: { "template": "response", "feedback_attempts": 2, "type": "clozeformula", "stimulus": "

What number makes the equation true?

\n\n

\\(5\\ =\\ \\square\\ \\div\\ 7\\)

\n", "validation": { "valid_response": { "value": [ [{ "method": "equivValue", "value": "35", "options": { "allowInterval": true, "allowThousandsSeparator": true, "compareGrouping": false, "ignoreCoefficientOne": false, "ignoreOrder": true, "ignoreTrailingZeros": true, "inverseResult": false, "setThousandsSeparator": [","], "setDecimalSeparator": ".", "decimalPlaces": 10 } }] ], "score": 1 }, "scoring_type": "exactMatch" }, "ui_style": { "validation_stem_numeration": "upper-alpha", "type": "no-input-ui" }, "is_math": true, "response_containers": [] } 2. Open the authored item in Preview mode. 3. Select the correct answer (35). 4. Select show correct answer. 5. Use NVDA screen reader with Speech Viewer enabled. Actual Result NVDA reads the correct answer redundantly, e.g.: “A - 35 - correct. A - 35 - correct. Response - correct.” This causes confusion and verbosity for screen reader users. NVDA should read the option once, clearly, and without duplication, e.g.: “Option A, 35, correct.” or “Answer A: 35 — correct.”

subject: Items API v2025.2 CSS Changes
raw_subject: Items API v2025.2 CSS Changes
description:
Hello, 

Our team is in the process of upgrading from the Items API v2024.2 to v2025.2 and we’ve encountered an issue with styling.

I’ve enclosed a screenshot. The left-hand side shows our app's appearance on our Production using v2024.2: a set of closed Accordion elements with the content hidden, which expand to show the Learnosity content when the user opens them. On the right-hand side, you can see how our app looks upgraded to v2025.2. Note how the Accordions start in a closed state as before, with the Learnosity content hidden; however, the content still takes up space within each Accordion element. When a user clicks to open any given Accordion header, the content then populates as normal. 

In investigating the issue, I see significant differences between the CSS present in Learnosity between the two versions. I’ve further looked into the differences by checking your migration guides and comparing versions of the CSS in github, which also appear to be substantial enough that it’s hard to go over in close detail: https://github.com/Learnosity/learnosity-apis-css/compare/lts/v2024.2.LTS..lts/v2025.2.LTS 

My questions are:
1) Is this an intentional change to the way the Item App's CSS works when embedded on a page? If not, is this a regression?
2) If this is an intended change, is there a canonical way to fully hide the Learnosity Items app and not have it create space within another element on the page until triggered to load?

I'm happy to provide any further information, screenshots, or code to share specifics about our issue.

Thanks,
Morgan

custom_fields.value: The customer is upgrading from Items API v2024.2 to v2025.2 and experiencing an issue where Accordion elements' content is hidden but still occupies space, unlike the previous version. They provided detailed configs, code snippets, and screenshots showing CSS discrepancies, suspecting a Learnosity CSS rule enforcing height and display properties. The support team could not reproduce the issue in a vanilla environment and suggested CSS workarounds like using display:none, but the customer prefers a proper fix in the API to avoid fragile hacks. The support team explained their sprint-based release cycle, estimating no fix before late September or October, and recommended a temporary workaround. The customer implemented a workaround that avoids direct Learnosity element manipulation and awaits a formal fix. Additionally, the customer raised concern about a broad CSS rule using :is(#lds, body) .collapse:not(.show) { display:none } that may unintentionally affect page elements outside Learnosity. Support acknowledged this and plans to escalate it to engineering, with the ticket added to backlog for future triage. The customer suggested narrowing the CSS selector to avoid affecting global page styles. No ETA for a fix is currently available; updates will be provided as progress occurs.

subject: imageAssociationv2 authoring questions
raw_subject: imageAssociationv2 authoring questions
description:
Our Science team is working on new development, and there are some question coming up around the imageAssociationV2 question type. The documentation on the Authoring site is very basic, and does not really do a good job of explaining how to develop these items with a high level of quality. I have re-created an example in our 1252 (Dev) environment - "ImageAssocitation_Questions" (NEW _196547e4-b139-479a-bce2-630f7ac41d22).
Questions the team has:
1. When you draw gaps on a background image and save, many times the gaps shift significantly, to where they have to-re-edit the question. Do you know why this happens?
2. The possible response images do not have any white padding around image. However, when you look at the preview of the question, there is a thin white border around images, which retain when you place them in response containers. Why does this happen, and can it be removed? It does seem to impact how the images fit in the container (resize or no).
3. Is there a max height and width on the question frame in Preview and in an activity? 
4. When you add background image, it is constrained in and does not scale up as the background image and response containers are scaled so while the preview resizes, the response images stay their original size. And since you scale by pixels and not percentage, it is difficult to get them aligned (for a basic author).
5. On response container creation, it is EXTREMELY difficult to get multiple containers to have the same dimensions only using the UI. Our authors do not have access to the source code, so they are hobbled by what can be done in the UI. It would be desireable to have UI boxes to specify the height, width and starting x,y for each container created (similar to way hotspot UI is set up to do global and individual styling).
6. Our Artist showed me how he built the art so the background image and the response images fit together perfectly, but when they are imported into Learnosity, they no longer align. In the example, the background image is shorter than the response images, even though they were created together so everything fit like puzzle pieces, so the response images shrink and create a gap at the bottom of the response container.

Overall, we would really like to utilize this question type more, but authors are frustrated with the UI and functionality, and tend to not choose it for their development. If there are any enhancments that are in the pipeline, we would like to know what they are.

A CSS workaround was provided but caused new problems with image scaling and dragger order. The vendor confirmed these are limitations due to responsive design and accessibility requirements, not bugs, and no immediate fixes exist. subject: Author API - preview - hint popup doesn't close on destroy()

We've observed some odd behavior in Author API when previewing questions with hints in the label image with math question type.

If you author a hint to the question and then preview it (whether in activity edit preview, item edit preview, or question edit preview) and click on the "Show Hints" button, then close the view in a manner that calls authorApp.destroy(), then Author API will be destroyed but the hint modal will remain.

3. Preview the question
4. Click the "Show Hints" button
5. Call authorApp.destroy()
6. Observe that the hint modal remains

Is this expected behavior?

Thanks!
Pierce

Shelly

subject: Use case for large file uploads
raw_subject: Use case for large file uploads
description:
Good morning, 

After some discussions around File Upload use cases, our Customer Success Manager, Nicola, has asked me to log a ticket here detailing the use case we have for larger file uploads.

Our use case centers around learner response uploads. By this, I mean a student uploading a file that will later be accessed by an exam marker for assessment. 

We have been approached several times recently by potential new clients who want to use our system. Some or all of their assessments involve some kind of project creation that must be submitted by the student.  

Some examples of this might be 
A video project (Recorded performances, video interviews, Final Cut projects, etc)
An audio project (high-fidelity live recordings / Pro Tools projects, etc)
A programming project 
Other project files exported from specific software (can vary - an example is a blender project)

Currently, we are aware of the 100MB file size limit that is in place for file uploads.

In our experience, this 100MB limit is too small for most of the project files listed above. 

As an example, a recent client required 2GB video files to be uploaded by students. Based on the number of uploads per year, the total would equate to 100TB per year. 

I am aware of the 5TB fair usage policy also, which would come into play here too in this specific example. However, this is probably a separate “issue”.  

There would be clients who may want to upload 2GB files but only to the amount of, say 300GB per year, so an increase in the file size would still be valuable even without impacting on fair usage policy. 

This is our use case for large file size uploads. I hope this provides some context, and if you have any other questions, please let me know. 

Thanks,
David

subject: Learnosity's Simple Features and Activity Player Template
raw_subject: Learnosity's Simple Features and Activity Player Template
description:
Hello there,

Reaching out to validate a potential solution or source alternative options. We have specific requirements to offer student-centric tools, such as a digital calculator, persistently throughout the entire assessment experience.

Upon investigation, we discovered that Learnosity offers various student-centric tools through Simple Features. We have identified the following requirements that align with these features:

- Ability to use a calculator
- Ability to use a digital line guide
- Ability to use a digital ruler
- Ability to use a digital protractor
- Ability to eliminate answer choices (masking)
- Ability to bookmark and review questions
- Ability to provide students with reference materials

To achieve these requirements, we explored creating a custom Activity Template using Simple Features. While we found that the template could include all the necessary tools, we encountered some limitations:

- The number of options displayed within the Activity Template seems limited (using vertical TOC and options on right-hand side).
- Resources seem limited to one per Activity.

We are considering the following options and need your guidance or alternative recommendations:

- Create a custom Activity Template
-- This approach included the user requirements but seemed limited in displaying multiple settings/tools in the feature container.

- Create several custom Activity Templates
-- This would be a longer-term solution. Paired with custom development enabling users to select functionalities and render the appropriate template based on the combination of their inputs.

- Resources 
-- Resource Items appear limited to '1' per Activity. Can that be adjusted to accommodate more? Are there alternative options we can explore?

Thank you for your assistance in advance!

Sincerely,

CJ Altman

subject: Feature request - Update File Upload item type to support Google Drive file extensions
raw_subject: Feature request - Update File Upload item type to support Google Drive file extensions
description:
Pearson is requesting that the File Upload type be updated to support Google Drive file extensions: 

.gdoc 

.gsheet 

.gslides 

 

Business context: Pearson is expanding support for Chromebooks. Virtual Schools expects up to 1/3 of our students to use Chromebooks starting in fall 2025, up from about 5% in the current school year. By 27-28, we expect all students to use Chromebooks instead of Windows devices.  

Google Drive does not natively allow students to save files in any of the Learnosity-supported File Upload formats; instead, the file has to be downloaded to local storage as a supported type, then re-uploaded. This adds an extra step for students to take when completing File Upload-type questions and is expected to be a reach for our younger (K-3) students. Additionally, this requires students to keep two versions of the file: one as their working copy in Google Drive and the other for submission in a different format. If teachers comment on the file and return it to the student to apply feedback, those comments will also be lost if the file is transferred back into Google Drive format. 

The average student will encounter File Uploads at least twice per semester in each core course, so 10 times per semester across a standard course load, in all grades. Given current enrollment of approx. 130,000 students, by the time all students are using Chromebooks, we expect approx. 2.6 million File Upload submissions per year from Chromebook devices.

subject: Learnosity Data API - Support for retrieving the total number of activities within an Item bank
raw_subject: Learnosity Data API - Support for retrieving the total number of activities within an Item bank
description:
Hello, 

At NE we have started to build a new Assessment delivery platform utilizing pretty much the full extent of the Learnosity API offerings. One of the features we are currently working on is an activity list page wherein users will be able to browse, search and preview activities in our item bank. 

We want this page to be paginated, wherein the user can see how many activities a given search query resulted in, and navigate sequentially by page number to view the next set of activities (arbitrary limit we have set currently is 9 activities per page).

The initial implementation of this feature utilizes the Data API to fetch activities by reference, tags and so forth. One issue we have encountered is that we do not find a good way in the Data API to find out how many total records a given getActivites query resulted in. 

We are aware there is pagination support in the limit and next token fields, but we won't know how many pages to render unless we can get a total on the amount of activities. In theory, we could set a very high limit in the metadata field (essentially fetching all activities), but we see this scaling very poorly as we can see us having thousands of activities in the future, resulting in enormous payloads, as well as rendering the next token useless. 

We would appreciate any guidance on whether there is an existing approach or workaround to retrieve a total count, or if this might be considered for a future enhancement to the API.

Kind regards,

Georg Grankvist
Software Developer 
Nationalencyklopedin

subject: Report on ADA issue
raw_subject: Report on ADA issue
description:
We have done a third party ADA analysis and received following feedback on drag and drop questions. Please check the feasibility of fixing this. Description A control's role conveys to assistive technologies the purpose - and expected interaction or effect - of the control. Using the correct role is important, as it helps assistive technology users to know what the control represents and therefore how to interact with the control. Almost all roles required by authors are covered by HTML or, in some cases, WAI-ARIA - there will usually already be an element or attribute already available within the specification for the developer to use. However, in a small number of cases, developers may need to create custom roles where no existing role exists. For example, HTML has no specific role for defining slides within a carousel or a presentation. To resolve this issue, WAI-ARIA introduced a new attribute called aria-roledescription which allows authors to an existing role with a custom one that is not explicitly defined in the HTML specification. Screen readers will then announce the custom role in place of the existing role when it encounters this attribute. The problem with this attribute is that its purpose is often misunderstood by web authors, which can result in content which would otherwise make sense being misunderstood by screen reader users. The aria-roledescription attribute is applied to the container element for items that can be dragged-and-dropped. Rather than indicate the role of the container (a region), it instead provides verbose instructions for the user, which is not the intended purpose of this attribute. User impact Screen reader users may therefore find it difficult to understand what they are interacting with when they reach this container. Required solution Only use the aria-roledescription attribute in cases where the existing role does not sufficiently encapsulate what the purpose of the related content is. The More Information section below provides additional guidance on when to use, and when not to use, this attribute. This solution must be applied to all instances of the issue identified within the test sample, then applied to all other instances of the same issue identified throughout the rest of the website. Implementation guidance This issue is best explained by way of an example. Draggable components in each of the drag-and-drop questions in the test sample are rendered inside a container that is correctly provided with role="region" and an aria-label attribute that describes the region. However, the container also includes an aria-roledescription attribute which is used to provide instructions for operating the underlying drag-and-drop functionality. This is not the intention of this attribute, and it means that the "region" rule is suppressed. To resolve this issue, remove the aria-roledescription attribute from the container
element. In terms of the instructions themselves, these are arguably useful for all users, so we strongly recommend that you provide them at the top of each question. Current markup:
... list of draggable components ...
Recommended markup:

Question

Label the organelles involved in the packaging and transport of lipids and proteins.

Provide your answer below ...

Instructions for using drag-and-drop

...instructions in here...

... drag-and-drop question ...
... list of draggable components ...

subject: Feature Request: Enhanced Audio Player for Accommodations and Play Count Display
raw_subject: Feature Request: Enhanced Audio Player for Accommodations and Play Count Display
description:
**Summary**

Berklee has highlighted a need for improvements in the Audio Player functionality within Atomic Assessments/Learnosity. These enhancements would support students requiring accommodations and improve transparency in exams that involve audio components.

**Current Behavior**

	1.	Berklee’s core exams use a 2-part item setup: a passage and an audio player.
	2.	The current setup does not allow custom accommodations for the number of audio playbacks, forcing Berklee to create multiple versions of exams for different accommodation needs.
	3.	The audio player does not display the playback limit to students. Instructors currently have to include this information manually in the passage text.

**Proposed Enhancements**

	1.	Customizable Play Count Accommodations:
	•	Allow instructors to set individualized playback limits for audio players per student or group, directly addressing accommodation requirements.
	•	Example: A standard playback limit of 3 for most students, with an accommodation allowing 5 playbacks for select students.
	2.	Student Playback Limit Display:
	•	Include a visible playback limit on the audio player interface for students.
	•	Example: “You have X playbacks remaining out of Y total” or a progress bar/ticker showing the remaining count.
	•	This will reduce confusion and eliminate the need for manual instructions in the passage text.

**Benefits**

	•	Simplifies exam setup for instructors, eliminating the need for multiple exam versions.
	•	Enhances accessibility for students requiring accommodations.
	•	Improves user experience by providing clear feedback to students on playback limits.

**Additional Notes**

	•	This request originates from Berklee, who are key users of Atomic Assessments and Learnosity’s Audio Player.
	•	These features would align with Universal Design for Learning (UDL) principles by ensuring equitable access to assessment materials.

**Priority**

Medium to High. Accommodations and accessibility are critical in academic settings, and these changes would significantly improve the assessment experience for both instructors and students.

subject: Learnosity Drag and Drop: Dialog boxes are missing role and name information
raw_subject: Learnosity Drag and Drop: Dialog boxes are missing role and name information
description:
Depending on the length of a draggable element's label text, not all of the text will be visible when dropped into a drop target. To get around this issue, the developers have provided a separate button that, when activated, displays a dialog box containing the full text, as well as a larger "droppable" target. 
 
Keyboard focus (correctly) moves into the dialog box when it appears on the page. However, the dialog box is not exposed as such to assistive technologies, and is missing an appropriate accessible name. Screen reader users who cannot see the page may wonder what has happened, and may not be aware that they have entered a dialog box.
 
When authoring the questions, there is an option called “Edit ARIA labels.” This ARIA label is applied to the Expand button inside the drop target, not to the dialog box. Therefore, using this option does not resolve the issue. The dialog box still lacks an appropriate accessible name and is referred to as a “toggle button,” which can confuse the user.
 
We are currently using Learnosity v2023.1 version and checked this using the both v2023.1 and v2024.3 versions in MacOS - Voiceover and Windows - Firefox - NVDA.

subject: unsupported Unicode escape sequence
raw_subject: unsupported Unicode escape sequence
description:
We are experiencing an "unexpected-exception" error with status code 500 and the message "unsupported Unicode escape sequence" when processing responses from Learnosity. This issue seems to occur when users copy and paste content from other websites that contains unsupported Unicode escape characters.

While we have implemented server-side validation to handle these characters, we believe a more robust solution could be achieved through collaboration and improvements within Learnosity itself.

Therefore, we would like to propose the following suggestions:

Return Parsed Answers: We kindly request that Learnosity return answers already parsed in cases where Unicode escape characters are present. This would eliminate the need for our backend to handle such parsing, simplifying our code and improving performance.

Client-Side Validation: Implementing input validation on the client-side within Learnosity would be highly beneficial. By ensuring that responses are parsed and validated before being sent to our backend, we can reduce the likelihood of encountering invalid Unicode characters and streamline response processing.

Review of Screen Keyboard: We recommend a review of the "screen keyboard" functionality to ensure that it does not allow the insertion of Unicode escape characters through any key combinations. Preventing the entry of unsupported characters at the source would significantly mitigate potential issues.

We believe that implementing these suggestions will enhance the robustness of our integration with Learnosity, improve the efficiency of our data-handling processes, and ultimately provide a better user experience.

subject: Video save fails, and students don't get any error warning until after submission
raw_subject: Video save fails, and students don't get any error warning until after submission
description:
A student submitted an error report for a submission on a video assignment where their most recently recorded video was almost 4 minutes long, but the submitted video was only about 1 minute. Upon further inspection, it looks like the video that got submitted was the one they had recorded previously. It looks like there was an issue with saving the video, but from the student's perspective they finished recording their new, longer video, clicked "Stop" saw the new video in the recording area, and clicked "Finish", but then the video that they had just made was not the one that actually got submitted. Our system then sent an error message after the submission saying that audio save to server failed, which is the only error message that it got from Learnosity, but by that time the attempt was submitted. 

Students should definitely see a warning before submitting an assignment if a video hasn't saved so that they can at least be aware that they're not submitting the most recent video at a point when they still have the ability to record a new one. I have attached a video of the logrocket session. 

The session ID was 6973ca32-fac3-4a12-bd32-2f99d0c1cb74.

description:
Hi Learnosity Support- this is in reference to the work in Zendesk ticket: Request #25864 HMH Multiple Organizations Thin Slice Testing Bulk Activity Updates incl. CSS

This issue appears in ORG: HMH Into Math and all these activities were included on the attached spreadsheet filename: Learnosity_Bulk_Update_Template_Math_K_6_LIVE

Please note the Resume & Exit button are enabled on Learnosity but do not appear on the activity itself until this is published to HMH Ed. 

1. Lunch URL: https://cert.hmhco.com/ui/login/?connection=92114880
2. State: Other
3. District: ZZ HMH Go Math K-6 National 2023-92114880
4. Username: Student1_92114881_cert
5. Password: E!4plutonium
6. Select the Assignments tab.
7. Click on the Start/Continue button of the "Chapter 3 Test: Compare Numbers" subject.
8. Click on the Save and Exit button.
9. Now select the "Resume button" of the Save and Exit dialog.
10. Observed that the Screen reader does not announce any updated information after clicking the 'Resume & Exit' buttons.

Note: This issue is observed for the Grades K-1 and 2-6
WCAG Guideline Number: 4.1.3

Refer to the attachment: GOMATHNA-2270.mp4

Actual result: Screen reader does not announce any updated information after clicking the 'Resume & Exit' buttons.

Rationale: Screen reader users are heavily dependent on the dictation conveyed by the screen reader. When dynamically updated content occurs on the page, even though the sighted users can understand the change, Screen reader users are solely dependent on the announcement of those changes. Hence, Alerts are used to convey such dynamic changes.

Recommendation: In order to make status messages accessible make sure to provide role=status to the container element of the alert.

Alternatively, provide an aria-live region using attributes such as aria-live="polite" to the status message. This will ensure that as soon as the status message is getting available on the page the same will be announced to the screen reader users.

Expected Result: Screen Reader should announce the updated information after clicking the "Resume & Exit" buttons.

subject: Undo/Redo Does Not Reflect Correct Operation Order in Text Editor
raw_subject: Undo/Redo Does Not Reflect Correct Operation Order in Text Editor
description:
Description:
When performing copy-paste operations in the text editor and then using the undo/redo controls, the behavior does not align with the expected order of operations. Specifically, the text editor incorrectly considers the originally written text as the modified element, rather than the pasted content.

Steps to Reproduce:
Open a question in the text editor.
Insert some text (e.g., "Test").
Copy the text using CTRL+C.
Paste the copied text in the same location using CTRL+V.
Use the Undo button from the controls.
Expected Behavior:
The pasted text should be recognized as the modified element and handled accordingly during the undo operation, reflecting the action sequence.

Actual Behavior:
The undo/redo controls treat the originally written text as the modified element, disregarding the pasted text.

Additional Information:
A video demonstrating the issue is attached to this report.

This behavior can lead to confusion and disrupt the editing workflow. It is likely a bug in how the text editor tracks or prioritizes operations for undo/redo.

subject: Interpretation of dates in item history when using the data API to update item content
raw_subject: Interpretation of dates in item history when using the data API to update item content
description:
I have a question regarding the interpretation of dates in the Item Bank author interface.

I'm looking at an item in particular in the 537 and 578 item banks: VR781996.  I was copying from Item Bank 537 to Item Bank 578 and we're seeing some inconsistencies in the dates.

I copied the item between item banks using the data API.  Calls are documented here: https://help.learnosity.com/hc/en-us/articles/18356478270109-itembank-endpoints-Data-API

The script first does a getItems, then getFeatures and getQuestions using the features[] and questions[] arrays, respectively, in this case from the 537 item bank.

Then I write the item to the 578 item bank, using setFeatures, setQuestions, and setItems, using the same exact JSON.

All API calls returned successfully. I'm using v2023.2.LTS version of the API.

When I look at the item list in the Learnosity Author Interface in the item bank I copied the item to (578), it will say the item is modified seconds ago.  However, if the item content didn't change, if I look at the Item History, it will say it was modified at an earlier time.

I did an experiment by adding a space to an item in the 537 item bank and copying the item to the 578 item bank.  In this case, the Item History does show the item was modified seconds ago.

Is it safe to say that if the item question, feature, or item content itself didn't change, if I view the item history, it will say the item was not modified?  

The list of items in the Author Interface will show the last time the item, questions, or features were updated via data API, no matter if there were changes to the item or contained objects or not?

I think I've seen it in the past if I update a feature on one item, the item list in the author interface will show that all items referencing that feature were updated, so I wanted to confirm that as well.

We're using this to QA that content was migrated between item banks so I wanted to clear this up.

I've included a couple screen shots showing an item's history and the same item in the Item List filtered to that item so you can see the discrepancy.  The two screenshots show the same item at the same point in time without any modifications and illustrates the different dates.

Thank you!

custom_fields.value: The customer is copying items between two item banks using the Learnosity Data API (v2023.2.LTS) and notices discrepancies in modification dates. Specifically, the item list in the Author Interface shows the item as modified seconds ago after a copy, even when no content changes occurred, while the Item History shows an earlier modification time. When actual content changes are made, both dates align. The customer wants to confirm if the item list update time always reflects the last API set call regardless of content changes, and if the Item History only updates when actual modifications occur. subject: Regarding Firefox Fullscreen Functionality and unintentional alliteration
raw_subject: Regarding Firefox Fullscreen Functionality and unintentional alliteration
description:
Hi,

We've run into a bit of a functionality error when it comes to fullscreening videos in a Learnosity item while using Firefox. All other browsers behave as expected.

The source of the bug seems to be weird behavior when pressing the escape key while the video is fullscreened. Clicking the fullscreen button works as expected, but pressing the escape key to exit fullscreen does not trigger the video to exit fullscreen. It appears that the browser knows to exit fullscreen, but the video does not, as shown in the screenshots of the video still in fullscreen. (If at a smaller screen size, there is CSS accounting for resizing the video, but it still behaves as if in fullscreen - note the placement in the top left instead of the center of the screen, and the fullscreen icon in the bottom right showing that it hasn't exited fullscreen.)

Upon further research, I learned that, for safety reasons, Firefox essentially hijacks any functionality away from the escape key while the browser is fullscreened. This is apparently to prevent malicious websites from triggering unwanted browser behavior. Unfortunately this prevents the escape key from allowing the video to exit fullscreen. Pressing the escape key a second time to attempt to exit fullscreen in the video causes the site to throw an error, because it sends an exitFullscreen event to a browser that is not fullscreen. This causes problems with some custom functions and CSS we've written inside some fullscreenchange event listeners; due to the exit function erroring, the video does not register the code we've written and instead stretches across the entire page.

As of right now we're not sure if there's any way around this. Is this something that's come up for Learnosity in the past? Would love to be able to move past this, as our website is meant to have best performance on Chrome and Firefox.

Thanks for reading. If there's any other information I can provide please let me know.

subject: Reports API Remote Control Pause Interrupts Submission

description:
Hello!

I would like to get clarification on a specific use case we're encountered with Learnosity, just to ensure we're not missing some method of improving the UX.

When a student reaches the end of an assessment, they can be configured to confirm submission via a Learnosity dialogue. While in this dialogue, the students test is paused.

So, a couple questions: 
* Is there any way to prevent the pause/resume operation from applying to the student who is already paused for the submit dialogue? (existing config, feature request/bug?)
* Are there events or API functions available to allow us to determine that the student is currently paused because of that submitting state in order to allow for the administrator application to avoid pausing students in that state?

Danny

subject: Seems to be no way to require simplified or factorized etc. answers in new Math question type
raw_subject: Seems to be no way to require simplified or factorized etc. answers in new Math question type
description:
With the old Cloze Math question type it was possible to set an answer as equivValue or equivSymbolic and then also set a requirement that it be isSimplified or isFactorised etc. This mean that you did not need to use EquivLiteral and come up with every possible order that students might use, i.e. figure out every possible order they might put a set of variables in and enter all of those as alternate answers, but you could still require that an answer be simplified, which was particularly useful on problems where students are given an equation and asked to simplify it, since often there are multiple orders that a simplified equation might end up in, so doing so is very time consuming, but if you set the question to allow equivValue or equivSymbolic they can just enter the original equation without actually simplifying it. This also means that if a student does something like putting a negative sign in the denominator or numerator instead of in front of a fraction, that answer is then marked incorrect, even though it has the same value, so that means that for answers that require a negative sign suddenly the number of answers needed is multiplied by three, when just needing to include every possible order of the elements had already ballooned the number of answers that needed to be set. Is this intentional? Is there a way to require that an answer be simplified so that one does not need to set so many answers or let students who have entered a correct answer in a slightly different order be marked incorrect? 

Here is an example of a question where this is an issue: https://practice.flatworldknowledge.com/editorial/books/125/chapters/6284/questions/2195529/edit?learnosity_question_id=2359669. The learnosity reference ID is a0152a8f-07aa-4a51-a318-c7dd9bac7d5c. A student has entered an answer as shown in the attached screenshot that has the negative on the denominator of the fraction, and so their answer has been marked incorrect, even though it is in fact simplified and equivalent to the set answer, because in order to make it so entering the original equation is not permitted the question has been set to "equivLiteral". Is there a way to make it so that this answer would be marked correct without manually adding it (and presumably also adding a version where the negative sign is in the numerator, and versions of those two formats and the original one where at least the y and z variables are swapped on the denominator, since even if we go with the convention that the coefficient of 125 should go first those variables can definitely be swapped without making an answer incorrect, so I think that the question would require a minimum of 6 set alternative answers), while making sure that the original function which has not been simplified (or another function that is equivalent and which might be reached along the path to fully simplifying the equation) would not be marked as correct?

custom_fields.value: The customer raised concerns about the new Math question type lacking the ability to require simplified or factorized answers, a feature previously available in the old Cloze Math type via equivValue or equivSymbolic with isSimplified/isFactorised checks. This limitation forces authors to manually enter many alternative answers to cover variable order and negative sign placement variations, increasing workload and risking marking correct answers as incorrect. Support acknowledged the issue, recommending using equivSymbolic with equivLiteral exclusions as a partial workaround but noted it is imperfect and cumbersome. Engineering confirmed this is a known issue planned for future development, though no timeline is available. The customer appreciates the attention and awaits updates.

subject: Issue with video feature UI disappering

description:
Good afternoon,

we have found a minor issue with the UI of the video feature. If an activity item is previewed as a participant, while a video feature is added, the video UI seems to disappear while the mouse cursor is hovering over the video.

The intended behaviour is that when the mouse cursor is hovering over the video, the video UI is present that shows the play button, time bar, full screen and volume options. When you move the mouse away from the video, the UI will disappear. This is intended.

If the user starts forwarding and rewinding the video while taking the mouse away from the video each time, you will find that when you go back to the video, the UI will not appear.

We have found that the UI will re-appear again after a little time, but the UI should always be present while hovering over the video.

Steps to replicate
- Create an activity
- Create an item
- Add a video feature
- Host video
- Save the Item
- Preview the Activity
- Play the video
- Forward the video
- Move the mouse cursor away from the video (Until the UI disappears)
- Rewind the video
- Move the mouse cursor away from the video (Until the UI disappears)
- Repeat these steps and you will see the UI will not reappear

On the attached video, the UI is instantly not available, this was on a Mac. I have found while testing on my Windows 11 machine that it happens after playing around with the video. subject: Formatting issue in Simple Chart
raw_subject: Formatting issue in Simple Chart
description:
I am working on translating our bar chart items from QTI to Learnosity json, and the formatting presents defects on the bar chart in Learnosity when certain options are selected. Specifically, creating a bar chart where at least one of the correct answers is less than a whole number. I have attached a number of screenshots that show the inconsistency between selections:

barchart_snaptogrid_blank: y-axis max= 16; no snap to grid value (chart autosizes to count by twos)
barchart_snaptogrid_1: y-axis max= 16; snap to grid value = 1 (chart still autosizes to count by twos)
barchart_snaptogrid_half: y-axis max= 16; snap to grid value = .5 (chart shows every value, becomes crowded)
barchart_max15_snaptogrid_1: y-axis max= 15; snap to grid value = 1 (chart counts by two until the last tic; no chart would ever be created this way)
barchart_max40_snaptogrid_half:  y-axis max= 20; snap to grid value = .5 (chart is unreadable)

I would expect consistency at a minimum - if snapto is 1 should show all increments of 1, like with .5; or continue with formatting, but allow snapto of .5 between the lines.

Ideally, we would like to be able to define the increment count:
barchart_ideal_rendering:  y-axis max= 16, increment (values defined on y-axis)=1, and snap to grid value = .5

Please let us know if an enhancement is already on the roadmap for the secondary request, or if a bug has already been reported for the first issue.

subject: XSS Vulnerabilities
raw_subject: XSS Vulnerabilities
description:
Hello,

I am a Software Engineer at Instructure working on its Mastery Connect software. We utilize the Learnosity Question Editor API for question authoring and utilize Bugcrowd for identifying security vulnerabilities in our app.

We've recently had some stored XSS vulnerabilities raised via Bugcrowd submissions related to the Learnosity Question Editor. The Learnosity Question Editor serves as the vector for the vulnerability, where the malicious actor enters the XSS injection attack and where the attack runs when the question is previewed by a user (teacher, student, etc.).

I've included the details that are relevant to Learnosity below, including a replication of the vulnerability that I was able to create within the Learnosity authoring portal.

---
Overview of the Vulnerability:

Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) is a type of injection attack where malicious JavaScript is injected into a website. When a user visits the affected web page, the JavaScript executes within that user’s browser in the context of this domain. When an attacker can control code that is executed within a user’s browser, they are able to carry out any actions that the user is able to perform, including accessing any of the user's data and modifying information within the user’s permissions. This can result in modification, deletion, or theft of data, including accessing or deleting files, or stealing session cookies which an attacker could use to hijack a user’s session.

Business Impact:

Stored XSS could lead to data theft through the attacker’s ability to manipulate data through their access to the application, and their ability to interact with other users, including performing other malicious attacks, which would appear to originate from a legitimate user. These malicious actions could also result in reputational damage for the business through the impact to customers’ trust.

Steps to Reproduce:

1: Login into https://author.learnosity.com
2: Create a new Math Formula Item.
3: Open the "More Options" panel.
4: In the More Options panel, you will see "Response minimum width (px)"
5: Put this XSS payload into it: "onmouseover=alert(document.domain)//
6: Click the button to preview the Item in the upper right corner.
7: Hover mouse over the response area to fire the XSS.
---

Though the original issue is identified on the Math Formula item type, the XSS vulnerability exists on other item types as well.

Additional Examples (non-exhaustive):
1. Math type item with injection payload on the "Width (px)" field.
2. Label Image with Math type with injection payload on the Response Container (global) “Height (px)” field.

We will be internally addressing how our application can sanitize these inputs, but we also wanted to raise the issue with Learnosity to ensure that the its team was aware of the vulnerability and so that we may receive updates on its resolution. Feel free to reach out to me directly at nic.nolan@instructure.com if you have any additional questions. Thank you for your time and we appreciate your help in this matter.

Best regards,

Nic Nolan

The vulnerabilities allow malicious JavaScript injection via fields like "Response minimum width (px)" in Math Formula items, executing when previewed by users. This poses risks of data theft, session hijacking, and reputational damage. Multiple item types are affected. Instructure will sanitize inputs internally but requested Learnosity's awareness and updates on resolution. Learnosity acknowledged the detailed report and escalated it to engineering and security teams for further action. No resolution timeline provided yet.

custom_fields.value: The customer is experiencing an issue where Google Translate correctly translates assessment content on first render in a React SPA, but fails to translate questions when switching to review mode or re-rendering. They have escalated the issue to engineering for further investigation but currently cannot offer a direct fix. The next step is awaiting engineering feedback on possible solutions or workarounds.

subject: Labels on choice-based question types
raw_subject: Labels on choice-based question types
description:
Labels associated to choices can be added in Choice and Hotspot question types. Why is the label attribute not available on other choice-like question types like Cloze Dropdown, or other question types where a student associates a choice to another object, like Cloze Association, Order List, and Image Association V2? 

Having to list an image uri or a string of text as a correct answer is problematic for our type of testing. 
Responses need to be consistent from year to year for high-stakes testing and accountability. If the location of the image changes between administrations, or if the text in the response is slighly modified, there is no longer continuity, and our psychometricians will have challenges with evaluating item responses between years, which is a necessary component of long-term use of items in high-stakes testing.

If New Meridian wanted to add in labels for the question types mentioned above, is there a way to do it without needing to create a custom version of each item type? Could this be added as a feature request? I would be willing to work with the Learnosity team to develop the specifications for the changes needed.

description:
If a table is put within a table, in the question text of any item made in the author tool, any text within the innermost table is rendered invisible if the participant enables "white on black" in accessibility tools. 

To replicate. 
1. Create activity
2. Create Item
3. Choose any question type
4. In "Question text" field press enter and click on table symbol to open "Table properties".
5. Click "Ok".
6. Click on table symbol again. 
7. Checkmark "Show borders".
8. Click "Ok" again.
9. Write text in each of the 6 columns in the table. 
10. Preview activity
11. Click on accessibility icon in right side of the window.
12. Select "White on black" and click "OK". 
13. Text in table should now be white, with the innermost table also being white, rendering the text invisible.

description:
New Meridian needs to support some specific use cases for authors that are not apparently available. subject: Error 500 when answering a session in behalf of student
raw_subject: Error 500 when answering a session in behalf of student
description:
Hello Support team!

As part of our efforts to improve our error handling we have identified a series of different scenarios that derive in Error 500 (Internal Error) scenarios.

Our purpose is to improve error handling and implement as graceful service disruption experience as possible for our users. (Similar to ticket: https://help.learnosity.com/hc/en-us/requests/23586 but unrelated)

In this particular case, a Teacher is attempting to answer a Student session on their behalf and thus we load the Learnosity Player exactly as a student would see it, so the teacher can complete the assessment.

However, in some cases, when prompted to re-evaluate the answers because of missing required numbers, if the user presses the "Cancel" button in the player modal's an uncaught exception happens.

Uncaught (in promise) undefined    score:10

We have attached a video of a reproduction of the issue, but please be aware that this is not necessarily the actions reported by our users, this is just the easiest way for us to reproduce the problem. 

What we have been reported with is normally the teacher progressing through the questions and making sure everything is correctly answered, until a certain point when they do miss an answer the "Cancel" prompt appears and that's when they get our 500 Internal error because of this exception.

Could you help us figure out what might be happening here?

Attached video, HAR file and screenshot.

Regards,
    Esteban

The act of applying font styling (e.g. bold, italics) is not announced to a screen reader, e.g. actions are happening that are unannounced. You can contrast this with Jira’s own rich text editor, in which clicking the “B” for bold after highlighting text causes the screen reader to read “Bold On”, and a second click to remove bold is announced as “Bold Off”

This isn't a huge issue for us, we don't plan to direct students to use styling as part of their responses, but we wanted to share our findings in case this is something you want to fix.

Thank you,

subject: Filtering "Find Existing Passages"?
raw_subject: Filtering "Find Existing Passages"?
description:
When searching for existing passages (Activity Edit view > Create Item > Find Existing Passage), is there a way to add additional default filtering?

We're filtering our items so that authors will only see items that are applicable for a given set of tags (https://reference.learnosity.com/author-api/initialization/config.item_list.filter.restricted.tags).  I know we can't have similar for passages, as you can't tag features, but is there any other ways to filter down the results that are shown by default?

A more concrete example of this use case:
1. One of the tags we filter our items on is ISBN so that instructors only see items for their adopted textbook
2. If the author searches for existing passages, they'll currently see passages for all textbooks, not just their adopted one

Is there a way that we can filter down the shared passages that show up so that, in this given use case, the author would only see the shared passages associated with their adopted textbook?

subject: Error message regarding non-zero-indexed arrays
raw_subject: Error message regarding non-zero-indexed arrays
description:
If you have a hash table of data, like this:

```
[
   7 => aaa-bbb-ccc
   11 => ddd-eee-fff
   99 => ggg-hhh-iii
]
```

and you try to feed it into `sessions/responses/scores`, you can get this:

```
Check session_id - must be an array
```

It's really asking me for a contiguous zero-indexed array, like this:

```
[
   0 => aaa-bbb-ccc
   1 => ddd-eee-fff
   2 => ggg-hhh-iii
]
```

To rectify that, you could amend the error message to something like 'Check session_id is a zero-index array' or just arbitrarily `array_values()` whatever I send to you.

On a similar note with `id` fields needing to be strings rather than ints, as Kit pointed out in some other ticket somewhere (I've lost track of which one)  - arbitrarily casting as string would help alleviate some misunderstandings.

subject: GM Internal Ticket - NEF-AMP383 / 382 Ensure active user interface components have sufficient contrast
raw_subject: GM Internal Ticket - NEF-AMP383 / 382 Ensure active user interface components have sufficient contrast
description:
A few contrast issues for the cloze with dropdown (student experience)

FIRST:

There are user interface components with a focus outline with a contrast ratio below 3.00:1.

Foreground color: #E8A420
Background color: #FFFFFF
Contrast ratio: 2.2:1

Examples of this user interface component include:

Temperature and Precipitation dropdowns

[User Impact]
Users with low vision will have difficulty identifying this content.

[Code Reference]
<select aria-label="Select cooler or warmer" class="lrn-cloze-select lrn_cloze_response" data-inputid="0" placeholder="Select cooler or warmer">

[Steps to reproduce]
1. Dock the web developer tools to the side of the browser window and resize the browser viewport until 320CSS pixels are shown.
2. Browse through the page until reaching the interactive element using the TAB key.
3. Open the browser console and inspect the element.
4. On the "Style" tab click the "toggle element state" button and select the ":focus" checkbox.
5. Copy the color code on the "Style" tab.
6. Use any contrast measuring tool like https://www.levelaccess.com/color-contrast-checker-new/ to measure the contrast ratio.

WCAG Rule: 1.4.11

[Recommendation]
Ensure active user interface components have sufficient contrast. The required minimum contrast ratio is 3.00:1.

Common examples of qualifying components include text field borders, check marks for checkboxes, fillings for radio buttons, focus indicators, and icon-only controls.

For borders, the "adjacent color" can be the color that touches the outside of the border or the color that touches the inside of the border. Contrast with both is not required.

Disabled controls that cannot be navigated to with the keyboard are exempt from this requirement.

Refer to the Accessible Color Picker extension or Color Contrast Checker site for assistance: https://www.accessibility.dev/

Are you sure you want to skip this item?

Choose Cancel to go back to the item.
Choose Continue to keep going and leave your answer blank.
[Steps to Reproduce] 1. Navigate through the website until reaching the specified element. 2. Inspect the element. 3. Notice how the element doesn't have an accessible name defined. WCAG Rule: 4.1.2, 1.3.1 [Recommendation] Ensure dialogs use proper structure. Dialog containers must have role="dialog". If the dialog has a visible title, set aria-labelledby on the dialog container to the ID of the visible title. For dialogs without a visible title, set a descriptive aria-label on the dialog element. [Compliant Code Example]

Are you sure you want to skip this item?

...
We consider this a high priority issue for us given the frequency of use of this modal. Mikaela

subject: Manipulate the length of the exam on initialisation
raw_subject: Manipulate the length of the exam on initialisation
description:
Submitted on behalf of David O'Neill at Better Examinations - follow-up from #22365

* * *
My second question raises a more serious security concern I have about how the client-side and backend interact. In doing some investigation on this, I discovered that the client does not seem to validate the response from, for example, the items api, to ensure that it has not been manipulated.

As an example, when I sit an exam, your client makes a request to https://items-ie.learnosity.com/v2022.2.LTS/activity?....

It returns a response object that contains many things, which include the max_time and the current_time.
I was able to simply intercept this response and modify the max_time to whatever I wanted. Your client then accepts this and your timer behaviors in accordance with whatever value I set for max_time in the manipulated response body.

Here, I am just manipulating max_time, but I'm assuming I can manipulate the entire response.

I'm very concerned that this leaves your client open to 'Man in the middle' attacks but, in general, leaves the possibility for any keen networking student (or otherwise), to very easily manipulate the Learnosity client by doing a simple network intercept and modifying the response.

When it comes to very high-stakes values, such as exam time, this is quite worrying for us.

Do you have any way of preventing such scenarios from occurring?

I have linked a guided recorded video explaining how I am able to manipulate the length of the exam on initialisation. The video file was too large to attach to this ticket
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1P6yguhmo55O7na74wnPBn1qNuc0ONNFF/view?usp=sharing
`"session_id": "2a6533be-c106-4362-9dee-294246296ae1"`

raw_subject: STXP - 200%/400% - Assessment - Axe Tools > Learnosity Hamburguer menu Aria Dialog issues
description:
We have submitted tickets closely related to this issue in the past but felt we needed to submit this one as well. This issue can be triggered with any assessment. In order to reproduce it, you only need to open the assessment hamburger menu with 200% or 400% zoom on, and run the axe tools scan (With the hamburger menu opened). We have assigned some assessments to the mentioned student user (below). 

Log in as a Student with an active Assessment (firststxp@yopmail.com / Test@123).

Teacher user (stxpte1@yopmail.com / Test@123 ; can assign an Assessment throw Assess: Great Minds Library | Assess | Great Minds Digital).

Student user with data created in STAGE environment: firststxp@yopmail.com / Test@123 (only active until June 3rd).

Assesss URL :  https://digital.stage.greatminds.dev/student/assessment/cb027377-4f49-4a14-b2b5-37d9b0d9c40f

1. Open an assessment on the Home page

2. Visualize the UI with 200% zoom (1366x768) zoom or 400% (320x256) zoom applied.

3. Open the Hamburger menu

4. Run Axe tools scan 

Actual Result
Several issues for the scenario are found:

-Aria dialog and alertdialog nodes should have an accessible name (opened hamburger menu).
.lrn-menu-region attribute does not exist or is empty.
-Frames must have an accessible name
iframe:nth-child(15) and iframe:nth-child(16).
-ID attribute value of element <textarea tabindex="0" class="lrn_focusable" id="focusable0formulaeditor0" aria-label="Response area" autocomplete="off" autocapitalize="none"></textarea> must be unique.
-Aria rol should be appropriate for the elements (opened hamburger menu)
<li tabindex="0" class="item-card lrn-assess-review-not_attempted  - role link must be removed when the elements are made visible, as it is not allowed for the elements.

Expected Results:
-Axe tools report no mayor issues for the assessment page in all views and layouts. 
-Ensure all <iframe> and <frame> elements have an accessible name
-Ensure every id attribute value of active elements is unique
-Ensure every ARIA dialog and alertdialog node has an accessible name
-Ensures role attribute has an appropriate value for the element

description:
OBSERVED RESULTS:

The "set correct answers" tab panel with tabs 'correct, alternate 1, alternate 2...' do not provide any context of tab panel. Programmatically it is not structured as a tab panel.
Screenshot
EXPECTED RESULTS:

A tab panel should have a clear name that indicates its name, purpose and state of selection.
To address this issue, add the necessary ARIA attributes to the tab panel, including:
Set the role attribute of the parent element to "tablist".
Set the role attribute of each individual tab to "tab".
Add an aria-selected attribute to each tab to indicate its active/inactive status.
Set the aria-controls attribute of each tab to the ID of the panel it controls.
Add a clear and concise aria-label attribute to the tab panel that describes its purpose.
The state of each tab (e.g., selected or unselected) should be indicated visually and with appropriate ARIA attributes.

Enable screen reader
Navigate to and activate any of the assessments you've created.

description:
Original ticket raised by Allain Dollete at Learnosity

**Affected APIs & Versions**
Items API

Presales client but tested on developer

Items API reset does not fully set the DOM hook back to its previous state

In our document, I states that the Items API reset method should remove all rendered items from the DOM.

**Priority context**
Low

**Client Context**
Presales client discovered this but raising internally.


> We are using the reset method on the ItemsApp object when unloading the component containing your player from the page. It states in your documentation that all rendered items from the DOM are removed. However we can see that you still leave the element in which your player gets injected classes and styling that gives the element height and width.

3. Inspect the DOM and observer the DOM hook

DOM element should only contain what was previously there before the Items API init

**Actual Behaviour**
DOM element still has properties that was added when Items API was initialized

**Developer Suggestion**

subject: Ipad: Issue with authoring items and item order
raw_subject: Ipad: Issue with authoring items and item order
description:
Hi Learnosity support,

We have found an issue related to the use of tablets (we specifically used an Ipad to test this, other tablets might give a different result).

When you have created an item with at least 2 questions in it, you should be able to change the order of the questions within it by using the 4 dots symbol on the right. However on ipads, whereever you click on the question (does not have to be on the 4 dots symbol) it will initiate the drag'n'drop by picking up the question.

When trying to release the question, nothing changes. Using the 4 dot symbol to try and change the order does nothing as well.

So the issue is two-fold:
1. trying to scroll by dragging your finger across the tablet will wrongfully make the tablet think you want to change question order (Making you unable to scroll down through your questions)
2. Drag'n'drop or 4 dot symbol order changing does not change the order at all on tablets. This functionality does not seem to work.

We have replicated this both on our own implementation of the authoring tool and your available Learnosity demoes.

Replication steps with tablet/ipad:
- Create item
- add 2 questions to item
- try to scroll/drag your finger along the questions when viewing the item
- See that it tries to change the order of questions, but never succeeds.

I hope the above explains the situation. Do let me know if you have any questions regarding any of the above or if you require any more information from us.

Have a nice day.

subject: [EM Student Assessment Audit] - Ensure frame titles are meaningful for short answer
raw_subject: [EM Student Assessment Audit] - Ensure frame titles are meaningful for short answer
description:
[Issue]
There are <iframe> elements without an accessible name for short answer.

[User Impact]
Screen reader users will have difficulty determining the purpose of these iframes.

[Code Reference]
<iframe style="width: 0px; height: 0px;" src="https://events.learnosity.com/v2022.1.LTS/xdomain" marginheight="0" marginwidth="0" frameborder="0" class="x-origin-frame"></iframe>

[Recommendation]
Ensure frame titles are meaningful. All meaningful iframes must have a title attribute set to a short description of the iframe.

[Compliant Code Example]
Example 1:
<frame src="frame1.html" title="Navigation Bar">

Example 2:
<frame title="Global Navigation" ...>
<frame title="Contextual Navigation" ...>
<frame title="Main Content" ...>

<!-- an non-user facing iframe -->
<iframe src="test.html" name="adventure" title="empty"
aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1" height="0"
width="0" />

subject: [EM Student Assessment Audit] - Ensure color is not the sole means of communicating information
raw_subject: [EM Student Assessment Audit] - Ensure color is not the sole means of communicating information
description:
[Issue]
There is content that uses color alone to visually indicate information. Examples include:
-Color alone used to distinguish between user and system created points

[User Impact]
Users with color blindness will have difficulty identifying the colors used to convey this information.

[Recommendation]
Ensure color is not the sole means of communicating information. Color can be used as long as other visual indicators of the information are also present. Common additional visual indicators include underlining, bolding, additional on-screen text conveying the information, or change in shape or size.

subject: [EM Student Assessment Audit] - Avoid improper nesting of form elements and links
raw_subject: [EM Student Assessment Audit] - Avoid improper nesting of form elements and links
description:
[Issue]
This DIV with a role attribute value of 'menu' should not contain input elements (without an assigned ARIA role), button elements (without an assigned ARIA role), textarea elements (without an assigned ARIA role), select elements (without an assigned ARIA role) or A elements (without an assigned ARIA role)

[User Impact]
Improperly nesting elements can hinder assistive technologies and users as they will not know how to interpret these components.

[Code Reference]
<div role="menu" class="lrn_dropdown_menu "/><div class="lrn_viewport"/><div class="lrn_viewport_content"/><button tabindex="0" unselectable="on" type="button" class="lrn_btn lrn_dropdown_option lrn_selected" aria-label="l a b e l" title="l a b e l"/><span class="lrn_content"/>label</span/></button/></div/></div/></div/>

[Recommendation]
Ensure all elements are properly formed. This means, if the link element is not required, then remove it and keep the input form elements only, and likewise, if the input form elements are not needed, keep only the link element (must review your component to understand the intended behavior - link elements are intended to take users to new pages whereas input form elements take user inputs).

subject: Error when validating math
raw_subject: Error when validating math
description:
We have a student who entered invalid math which is causing Learnosity to display an exception when they attempt to resume the attempt.  

To reproduce, create the attached question. As a student enter "1/^2x" and click check answer. Learnosity raises the exception 

"(10019) Failed validating math
    e is undefined Failed validating user input '\frac{1}{^{2x' against validation object: method: undefined" 
 
There are two issues here I think:
1. An exception shouldn't be raised.  The question should just fail validation.
2. The student should see that the answer is invalid.  As it is they see \frac{1}{2x} and the only clue that something is wrong is that the font size of 2x is a little small. We would expect some visual indication of a missing base to the exponent.

Thanks! -matt

subject: ADA Issues
raw_subject: ADA Issues
description:
We are encountering some issues regarding the ADA features within Learnosity.

In the creation window, after pasting from an external, unformatted document, we usually cut the text to paste into the answer choices below the initial question portion. We have discovered when you cut or copy within Leanosity, then paste the text within Learnosity anywhere, it will paste with a white background attached, which was not present before. We do this action regularly when creating items within the creation feature. Attached is the source code for one of these items, which somehow gained a background after it had been put into Learnosity. 
So the issue is that it is causing an issue with the ADA Color schemes available, as it does not go away once an ADA choice is selected (attached). Upon further testing, we also realized that any Activity Subtitle which is set is entirely unable to be seen or is greatly difficult to see with two of the Color schemes: Yellow on Navy and White on Black.

Additionally, Activity Subtitles are difficult or impossible to read in certain color schemes (Yellow on Navy, White on Black). Attempts to reproduce the issue were inconsistent; a video was provided for clarity. The text background issue is escalated to engineering for investigation. The subtitle visibility problem is linked to the rich text editor; switching to CKEditor is expected to resolve it. No final resolution yet; awaiting engineering feedback and CKEditor deployment.

subject: Adding organisation_ids to activity definitions via the Source panel can generate an IBK access error
raw_subject: Adding organisation_ids to activity definitions via the Source panel can generate an IBK access error
description:
Original ticket raised by Rich Shupe at

**Affected APIs & Versions**
Author API All

**Issue**
If an author adds items to the activity editor Source panel, or an activity has been defined via the Data API using items, from an additional org that is not part of the Author API initialization request object, a descriptive but not entirely useful error is logged in the console, and ill effects such as a permanent spinner and limited functionality can occur (this latter part has not been thoroughly tested).

Example A:

1. Consumer has access to orgs 1 through 4.
2. Author API is initialized using orgs 1 and 2.
3. Adding items from 1 or 2, even in the Source panel (if done using the correct syntax) will work.
4. But adding an item from org 3 in the Source panel (not possible in the UI) will break the Author API instance.

Example B:

1. Consumer has access to orgs 1 through 4.
2. Customer regularly creates activities using a mixture of orgs.
3. Customer regularly initializes the Author API with different additional orgs in the request object (perhaps for specific departments, authors, projects, etc.)
4. If authors work only with the activities created using that configuration, all is well.
5. But if an activity created with a different configuration of additional orgs is loaded, the Author API instance breaks.

**Priority context**
Normal

**Client Context**
Normal

**Steps to Replicate**
1) Go to this demo: https://demos.learnosity.com/authoring/activity-edit-multi-ibk.php

2) Add any item from either item bank to an activity.

3) Go to the Source panel and add this to the items array:

    , {
            "id": "EL421835074",
            "reference": "EL421835074",
            "organisation_id": 464
        }

This item was chosen because Learnosity Demos currently has access to that item bank, but the Author API was only initialized with access to the primary and one additional org, not 464. You can also use an org id that a consumer doesn't have access to or is outright wrong, but this is not required. Supported use cases without obvious errors still cause the problem.

4) Try to Apply and you'll get an endless spinner affecting work elsewhere in the instance.

5) Open the console and see the following error.

    {
        "status": false,
        "timestamp": 1630376915,
        "code": 20003,
        "message": "Requested item bank is not available",
        "request_uuid": "b2d4fc65-2401-4a4f-9834-22f8260b72e7",
        "consumer_name": "learnosity-demos",
        "versions": {
            "requested": "v2021.2.LTS",
            "mapped": "v1.83",
            "concrete": "v1.83.2"
        }
    }

6) You can also create an activity definition with the Data API that references additional org_ids that have not been added to the Author API init, and try to open that activity.

7) You can also create an activity using two supported orgs and then reload the Author API with a different set of additional orgs in the config, and then open the activity again.

Please let me know if you need more info here.

**Expected Behaviour**

1) Provide a list of org ids that the Author API's current config doesn't have access to.
2) Hide the spinner
3) Don't hinder use of any other features (this has not been thoroughly tested).

Beyond that is debatable. Ideally, we can issue a warning before any other edits are attempted. In that case, we might prevent a save. However, if that's not sure to work, I'd suggest we allow the user to edit/save but (again, ideally) just display the error and block the preview. We're open to discussion at this point.

**Actual Behaviour**
Spinner remains visible, Correct but not fully descriptive console error logged.

subject: Potential memory leak within authoring
raw_subject: Potential memory leak within authoring
description:
I've noticed anecdotally that the authoring interface gets slower over time when in a large editing session.  We've also had reports of this from instructors.  Question authoring will get slow over time, and closing and reopening the browser window will fix the problem.

I did the following test: 
I created an item with a single multiple choice item and then repeatedly clicked the "pencil" to edit the question and "back" to go back to the item.  Each time I did this the memory usage reported in Chrome dev tools seemed to climb ~7 MB. Sometimes it went down a bit, but over time it grew.  After quite a few iterations it was using 500MB of space.  I suspect that this might be related to (or a side effect of) whatever is causing the slow down over time.

I see the exact same behavior on author.learnosity.com
